options.text: A temporary absence of ovarian ovulation

options.text: A reduction in growth hormone as the cause of tissue overgrowth

options.text: Excess growth hormone with increased IGF-I activity

options.text: Bone thinning guarantees that blood calcium must also be low

options.text: The parathyroid glands produce the same hormones as the thyroid gland
options.rationale: The similarly named glands have different functions. Parathyroid glands produce PTH, which regulates calcium balance.

options.text: PTH always lowers blood calcium by locking all calcium into bone

stem:

Additional Information: Double-check and verify medication calculations. Incorrect calculation of medication dosages causes medication errors that can compromise patient safety.

options.rationale: Check and verify allergies: Always ask the patient about their medication allergies, types of reactions, and severity of reactions. Verify the patient’s medical record for documented allergies. The description in the question instead matches Be diligent and perform medication calculations accurately.

options.text: Be diligent and perform medication calculations accurately
options.rationale: The matching entry is Be diligent and perform medication calculations accurately. Additional Information: Double-check and verify medication calculations. Incorrect calculation of medication dosages causes medication errors that can compromise patient safety.

options.text: Perform appropriate patient assessments before medication administration
options.rationale: Perform appropriate patient assessments before medication administration: Assess the patient prior to administering medications to ensure the patient is receiving the correct medication, for the correct reason, and at the correct time. For example, a nurse reviews lab values and performs a cardiac assessment prior to administering cardiac medication. See more information regarding specific patient assessments during parenteral medication administration in the “Applying the Nursing Process” section. The description in the question instead matches Be diligent and perform medication calculations accurately.

options.text: Use available technology to administer medications
options.rationale: Use available technology to administer medications: Use available technology, such as bar code scanning, when administering medications. Bar code scanning is linked to the patient’s eMAR and provides an extra level of patient safety to prevent wrong medications, incorrect doses, or wrong timing of administration. If error messages occur, it is important to follow up appropriately according to agency policy and not override them. Additionally, it is important to remember that this technology provides an additional layer of safety and should not be substituted for the checking the five rights of medication administration. The description in the question instead matches Be diligent and perform medication calculations accurately.

A pathogen that can cause disease in a host regardless of the host’s resident microbiota or immune system.

Specific adaptive immunity: The immune response that is activated when the nonspecific innate immune response is insufficient to control an infection. There are two types of adaptive responses: the cell-mediated immune response, which is carried out by T cells, and the humoral immune response, which is controlled by activated B cells and antibodies. The description in the question instead matches Primary pathogen.
Primary pathogen is the matching concept. In this reference context: A pathogen that can cause disease in a host regardless of the host’s resident microbiota or immune system.

stem:
Which entry in the reference comparison “Common Diagnostic Tests for Nervous System Disorders” matches this information?

Description and Indication: X-rays of the spinal cord and vertebral column are taken after contrast is injected into the subarachnoid space. Used to detect spinal lesions and/or CSF leaks.

options.rationale: Carotid artery duplex scan: Combines ultrasound and Doppler technology to evaluate the degree of stenosis (narrowing) of the carotid and vertebral arteries. Using transducer gel, a probe is placed over the common carotid artery and moved slowly along its length. Frequency of reflected ultrasound signal corresponds with the velocity of blood flow. Increased blood flow velocity may indicate stenosis or partial or total occlusion of the vessels. The description in the question instead matches Myelogram.

Electroencephalography: Electrodes are placed on the scalp to record electrical activity of the cerebral hemispheres. Each graphic recording represents electrical impulses within the brain. The frequency, amplitude, and characteristics of the brain waves are recorded to evaluate seizure disorders, cerebral disease, brain injury, and brain death. The description in the question instead matches Myelogram.

The matching entry is Myelogram. Description and Indication: X-rays of the spinal cord and vertebral column are taken after contrast is injected into the subarachnoid space. Used to detect spinal lesions and/or CSF leaks.

Magnetic resonance imaging: Provides imaging of the brain and spinal cord by using magnetic energy to detect strokes, multiple sclerosis, tumors, trauma, seizures, and brain herniation. Produces greater detail than CT with improved detail of intracranial structures, but the procedure takes longer to complete and may not be appropriate if a client is experiencing a life- threatening emergency.; Contrast agents, such as gadolinium, can be used with MRI to enhance visualization. The description in the question instead matches Myelogram.

rationale: The matching entry is Myelogram. Description and Indication: X-rays of the spinal cord and vertebral column are taken after contrast is injected into the subarachnoid space. Used to detect spinal lesions and/or CSF leaks.

stem:
Which entry in the reference comparison “Blood Products, Used for life-threatening hemorrhage where oxygen-carrying capacity, coagulation factors, platelets, and volume expansion are all needed. Whole blood contains approximately 150 mL of plasma, which provides volume expansion and stabilization of clotting factors.” matches this information?

Actions/Indications/Benefits: Provides patient’s own blood to prevent potential transfusion reactions but has risk for bacterial infection. Used to replace blood loss during planned elective surgery.

options.rationale: Fresh Frozen Plasma: Increases clotting factors and expands blood volume. Indicated for clients with bleeding disorders, thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP), and life-threatening hemorrhage in patients who have significant coagulation deficiencies. Also used to reverse a client’s elevated INR when it needs to be brought down quickly to prevent complications from occurring. One unit increases clotting factors approximately 2-5%. Plasma is typically frozen within hours of donation to preserve the clotting factors and is thawed by the lab prior to administration. The description in the question instead matches Autologous.

The matching entry is Autologous. Actions/Indications/Benefits: Provides patient’s own blood to prevent potential transfusion reactions but has risk for bacterial infection. Used to replace blood loss during planned elective surgery.

Cryoprecipitate: Provides Factor VIII, fibrinogen, vWF, and Factor XIII. Indicated for Hemophilia A, von Willebrand’s disease, and Factor XIII deficiency. Also used as a part of “Mass Transfusion” protocols where clotting factor deficiencies are common. One pool increases fibrinogen approximately 50 mg/dL. The description in the question instead matches Autologous.

Leukocyte-Reduced RBCs: Indicated for symptomatic anemia for patients who are immunocompromised or at risk for reactions caused by leukocyte antibodies to the HLA. It is also recommended for children younger than six years old. It has the same actions/benefits as RBC infusion. The description in the question instead matches Autologous.

rationale: The matching entry is Autologous. Actions/Indications/Benefits: Provides patient’s own blood to prevent potential transfusion reactions but has risk for bacterial infection. Used to replace blood loss during planned elective surgery.

Description: A transgender parent is a parent who identifies as a different gender from their biological gender. A transgender parent may transition to a different gender prior to or after having a child.; View a supplementary Vimeo video on care considerations for children of LGBTQIA families: Considerations for Children of LGBTQIA+ Families.

options.rationale: The matching entry is Transgender parents. Description: A transgender parent is a parent who identifies as a different gender from their biological gender. A transgender parent may transition to a different gender prior to or after having a child.; View a supplementary Vimeo video on care considerations for children of LGBTQIA families: Considerations for Children of LGBTQIA+ Families.

Adoptive families: Adoptive parents legally take a child into their family and raise them as their own because of infertility issues or because they prefer adoption. Adoption may be open or closed. Open adoption ranges from simply knowing the identities of the birth parent(s) to having a continued relationship with the birth parents as the child grows up. Closed adoption means the family does not have access to information about the birth parent(s) nor do birth parents have access to information about the adoptive family or child. The description in the question instead matches Transgender parents.

Children with incarcerated parent: One or both parents are incarcerated. The family’s structure, roles, and functions change when the incarcerated parent is away from home and again when the parent returns home. ▶ Read more information about the impact of incarcerated parents on children on the National Institute of Justice web page. The description in the question instead matches Transgender parents.

First-time older parents: Older parents in their 40s, 50s and older may have children for several reasons. For example, they may have chosen to first establish their career(s) and/or financial security, or they may have experienced infertility resulting in a delay in starting a family. In other cases, women may experience an unplanned pregnancy during perimenopause when they thought they could not conceive. The description in the question instead matches Transgender parents.

subject: NP4
stem:
Which entry in the reference comparison “Common Diagnostic Tests for Nervous System Disorders” matches this information?

Description and Indication: Measures metabolic activity of the brain to determine cell death or damage. A radioactive isotope is injected that shows up as a bright spot on the image if abnormal activity is occurring. Indicated for clients with stroke, Alzheimer’s disease, seizure disorders, Parkinson’s disease, infection, and tumors.

options.rationale: Carotid artery duplex scan: Combines ultrasound and Doppler technology to evaluate the degree of stenosis (narrowing) of the carotid and vertebral arteries. Using transducer gel, a probe is placed over the common carotid artery and moved slowly along its length. Frequency of reflected ultrasound signal corresponds with the velocity of blood flow. Increased blood flow velocity may indicate stenosis or partial or total occlusion of the vessels. The description in the question instead matches Positron emission tomography.

Electromyography: Records the muscle and nerve integration and electrical activity. Needle electrodes are inserted into the specific muscle units being tested. Normal, relaxed muscles show no electrical activity, and contracted muscles show electrical activity. The test is indicated for testing for muscle and nerve diseases. The description in the question instead matches Positron emission tomography.

X-rays: Simple X-ray images of the skull and spine are done to detect fractures, calcifications, bone erosion, and abnormal vascularity. The description in the question instead matches Positron emission tomography.

subject: NP4
stem:

Description and Indication: Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) is aspirated from the subarachnoid space by a health care provider by inserting a needle between L3-4 or L4-5. Used to examine CSF for infection or presence of blood and measure and reduce CSF pressure. Fluid should be clear and colorless. Pink or blood-tinged CSF may be a sign of subarachnoid hemorrhage, and cloudiness may be due to increased WBCs.

options.rationale: Electroencephalography: Electrodes are placed on the scalp to record electrical activity of the cerebral hemispheres. Each graphic recording represents electrical impulses within the brain. The frequency, amplitude, and characteristics of the brain waves are recorded to evaluate seizure disorders, cerebral disease, brain injury, and brain death. The description in the question instead matches Lumbar puncture.

Carotid artery duplex scan: Combines ultrasound and Doppler technology to evaluate the degree of stenosis (narrowing) of the carotid and vertebral arteries. Using transducer gel, a probe is placed over the common carotid artery and moved slowly along its length. Frequency of reflected ultrasound signal corresponds with the velocity of blood flow. Increased blood flow velocity may indicate stenosis or partial or total occlusion of the vessels. The description in the question instead matches Lumbar puncture.

The matching entry is Lumbar puncture. Description and Indication: Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) is aspirated from the subarachnoid space by a health care provider by inserting a needle between L3-4 or L4-5. Used to examine CSF for infection or presence of blood and measure and reduce CSF pressure. Fluid should be clear and colorless. Pink or blood-tinged CSF may be a sign of subarachnoid hemorrhage, and cloudiness may be due to increased WBCs.

Positron emission tomography: Measures metabolic activity of the brain to determine cell death or damage. A radioactive isotope is injected that shows up as a bright spot on the image if abnormal activity is occurring. Indicated for clients with stroke, Alzheimer’s disease, seizure disorders, Parkinson’s disease, infection, and tumors. The description in the question instead matches Lumbar puncture.

Intentional self-inflicted destruction of body tissue without suicidal intention and for purposes not socially sanctioned. Common forms of NSSI include behaviors such as cutting, burning, scratching, and self-hitting.

A state of well-being in which an individual realizes their own abilities, copes with the normal stresses of life, works productively, and contributes to their community.

A scrubbing device with an embedded alcohol product such as chlorhexidine with alcohol or 70% alcohol to disinfect catheter hubs or needleless connectors.

options.rationale: Aseptic-impregnated catheter hub: A specific device or product that has an aseptic particulate embedded within it to prevent biological contaminants from entering a susceptible host. Hemodynamic monitoring: The assessment of a critically ill client’s circulatory status and includes measurements of central venous pressure, cardiac output, and blood volume. The description in the question instead matches Scrub hub.

Locking: The injection of a limited volume of a liquid following the catheter flush, for the period of time when the catheter is not used, to prevent intraluminal clot formation and/or catheter colonization. The description in the question instead matches Scrub hub.

Consistency of verbal and nonverbal communication.

When a person experiences a persistent depressed mood or a significant loss of interest or pleasure in activities, and these symptoms are directly caused by a medical illness or condition.

options.rationale: Depressive disorder due to another medical condition is the matching concept. Major depressive episode: A period of at least two weeks during which a person experiences a persistently depressed mood or a loss of interest or pleasure in nearly all activities, most of the day, nearly every day. The description in the question instead matches Depressive disorder due to another medical condition.

Seasonal affective disorder: A type of depression causing symptoms during the fall and winter months when there is less sunlight and usually improves with the arrival of spring. SAD is more than just “winter blues.” The symptoms can be distressing and overwhelming and can interfere with daily functioning. The description in the question instead matches Depressive disorder due to another medical condition.

Group therapy: A type of psychotherapy that brings people with similar disorders together in a supportive environment to learn how others cope in similar situations. The description in the question instead matches Depressive disorder due to another medical condition.

In Urinary System Terminology, which concept matches this description?

The process in the kidneys where blood plasma is filtered through the glomeruli, allowing waste products and excess substances to be excreted while retaining necessary components.

options.rationale: Glomerular filtration is the matching concept. In this reference context: The process in the kidneys where blood plasma is filtered through the glomeruli, allowing waste products and excess substances to be excreted while retaining necessary components.
Diuresis: Increased or excessive production of urine, which can occur in various medical conditions. The description in the question instead matches Glomerular filtration.

options.rationale: The matching entry is Confronting. Examples: Client: “I haven’t drunk much this year.”; Nurse: “Yesterday you told me that every weekend you go out and drink so much you don’t know where you are when you wake up.”

Encouraging Comparisons: Nurse: “It must have been difficult when you went through a divorce. Additional Information: Follow a standardized procedure when administering medication for every patient. Look up current medication information in evidence-based sources because information changes frequently.

options.text: Use standard procedures and evidence-based references
options.rationale: The matching entry is Use standard procedures and evidence-based references. Additional Information: Follow a standardized procedure when administering medication for every patient. Look up current medication information in evidence-based sources because information changes frequently.

Ensure medication has not expired: Check all medications’ expiration dates before administering them. Medications can become inactive after their expiration date. The description in the question instead matches Use standard procedures and evidence-based references.

options.text: Follow agency policies and procedures regarding medication administration
options.rationale: Follow agency policies and procedures regarding medication administration: Avoid work-arounds. A work-around is a process that bypasses a procedure or policy in a system. For example, a nurse may “borrow” medication from one patient’s drawer to give to another patient while waiting for an order to be filled by the pharmacy. Although performed with a good intention to prevent delay, these work-arounds fail to follow policies in place that ensure safe medication administration and often result in medication errors. The description in the question instead matches Use standard procedures and evidence-based references.

options.text: Be diligent and perform medication calculations accurately
options.rationale: Be diligent and perform medication calculations accurately: Double-check and verify medication calculations. Incorrect calculation of medication dosages causes medication errors that can compromise patient safety. The description in the question instead matches Use standard procedures and evidence-based references.

stem:
Which entry in the reference comparison “Summary of Safe Medication Administration Guidelines” matches this information?

Additional Information: Use at least two patient identifiers before administration and compare information against the medication administration record (MAR).

options.text: Perform appropriate patient assessments before medication administration
options.rationale: Perform appropriate patient assessments before medication administration: Assess the patient prior to administering medications to ensure the patient is receiving the correct medication, for the correct reason, and at the correct time. For example, a nurse reviews lab values and performs a cardiac assessment prior to administering cardiac medication. See more information regarding specific patient assessments during parenteral medication administration in the “Applying the Nursing Process” section. The description in the question instead matches Use two patient identifiers and follow agency policy for patient identification.

options.text: Use two patient identifiers and follow agency policy for patient identification
options.rationale: The matching entry is Use two patient identifiers and follow agency policy for patient identification. Additional Information: Use at least two patient identifiers before administration and compare information against the medication administration record (MAR).

options.text: Communicate with the patient before and after administration
options.rationale: Communicate with the patient before and after administration: Provide information to the patient about the medication before administering it. Answer their questions regarding usage, dose, and special considerations. Give the patient an opportunity to ask questions and include family members if appropriate. The description in the question instead matches Use two patient identifiers and follow agency policy for patient identification.

options.text: Use available technology to administer medications
options.rationale: Use available technology to administer medications: Use available technology, such as bar code scanning, when administering medications. Bar code scanning is linked to the patient’s eMAR and provides an extra level of patient safety to prevent wrong medications, incorrect doses, or wrong timing of administration. If error messages occur, it is important to follow up appropriately according to agency policy and not override them. Additionally, it is important to remember that this technology provides an additional layer of safety and should not be substituted for the checking the five rights of medication administration. The description in the question instead matches Use two patient identifiers and follow agency policy for patient identification.

rationale: The matching entry is Use two patient identifiers and follow agency policy for patient identification. Additional Information: Use at least two patient identifiers before administration and compare information against the medication administration record (MAR).

Position in which the fetal buttocks (or legs) enter the pelvis first.

options.rationale: Breech presentation is the matching concept. In this reference context: Position in which the fetal buttocks (or legs) enter the pelvis first.

Perineal hygiene: May include pouring warm water over the perineum or using wet washcloths to cleanse the perineum moving from the pubic hair line to the anus using a front-to-back motion. A separate area of the washcloth should be used for each stroke to prevent contamination from the rectum to the vaginal area. The description in the question instead matches Breech presentation.
Footling breech: Breech position in which the fetus presents one leg first. The description in the question instead matches Breech presentation.

Uterine tachysystole: Refers to more than five uterine contractions in ten minutes or a contraction length of two or more minutes within a 30-minute period. The description in the question instead matches Breech presentation.

rationale: Breech presentation is the matching concept. In this reference context: Position in which the fetal buttocks (or legs) enter the pelvis first.
keyPoint: Breech presentation: Position in which the fetal buttocks (or legs) enter the pelvis first.

subject: NP5
stem:
Which entry in the reference comparison “Common Types of Urinary Incontinence” matches this information?

Cause: Involuntary contractions of the bladder muscles cause an urgent need to urinate. Bladder irritants like caffeine, artificial sweeteners, and nicotine are also causative factors.

options.rationale: The matching entry is Urge Incontinence. Cause: Involuntary contractions of the bladder muscles cause an urgent need to urinate. Bladder irritants like caffeine, artificial sweeteners, and nicotine are also causative factors.
Stress Incontinence: Weakened pelvic floor support from factors like childbirth, pelvic surgeries, obesity, or hormonal changes. The description in the question instead matches Urge Incontinence.
Overflow Incontinence: Bladder outlet obstruction (e.g., enlarged prostate) or nerve damage affecting bladder contraction. The description in the question instead matches Urge Incontinence.
Functional Incontinence: Arthritis, dementia, or decreased mobility. The description in the question instead matches Urge Incontinence.

rationale: The matching entry is Urge Incontinence. Cause: Involuntary contractions of the bladder muscles cause an urgent need to urinate. Bladder irritants like caffeine, artificial sweeteners, and nicotine are also causative factors.

In Healthy Newborn Care, which concept matches this description?

Benign vascular tumors that appear as raised, red marks on the skin. They may grow in the first months of life but typically shrink and disappear by age 10.

options.rationale: Shunts: A term for alternative circulatory pathways that allow blood to bypass the lungs and liver until birth. The description in the question instead matches Hemangiomas.

Apgar score: A tool used to evaluate how well the newborn is tolerating the transition from fetal to neonatal circulation. The description in the question instead matches Hemangiomas.

Plantar grasp reflex: Similar to the palmar grasp but occurs when pressure is applied to the sole of the foot, causing the toes to curl under. The description in the question instead matches Hemangiomas.

rationale: Hemangiomas is the matching concept. In this reference context: Benign vascular tumors that appear as raised, red marks on the skin. They may grow in the first months of life but typically shrink and disappear by age 10.

Slough: Inflammatory exudate in wounds that is usually light yellow, soft, and moist. The description in the question instead matches Nonblanchable erythema.

Braden Scale: A standardized assessment tool used to assess and document a client’s risk factors for developing pressure injuries. The description in the question instead matches Nonblanchable erythema.

Interventions that are carried out by having personal contact with a client.

The study of the social, cultural, psychological, cognitive, and biological aspects of aging.

SPICES tool: Focuses on areas of common problems for aging individuals and can lead to early intervention and treatment. The description in the question instead matches Gerontology.
Ageism: The stereotyping and discrimination against individuals or groups on the basis of their age. The description in the question instead matches Gerontology.

subject: NP4
stem:
In Muscular System Terminology, which concept matches this description?

The act of turning the palm downward or when applied to the foot, the inward roll of the foot/ankle.

options.rationale: Pronation is the matching concept. In this reference context: The act of turning the palm downward or when applied to the foot, the inward roll of the foot/ankle.

Rotator cuff: A group of muscles and tendons surrounding the shoulder joint, keeping the head of the humerus firmly within the shallow socket of the shoulder. The description in the question instead matches Pronation.
Dorsiflexion: The backward flexion or bending of a hand or foot. The description in the question instead matches Pronation.
Dysarthria: Slurred or slow speech that can be difficult to understand. The description in the question instead matches Pronation.

rationale: Pronation is the matching concept. In this reference context: The act of turning the palm downward or when applied to the foot, the inward roll of the foot/ankle.

A short session to share a plan, discuss team formation, assign roles and responsibilities, establish expectations and climate, and anticipate outcomes and contingencies.

Assignment: Routine care, activities, and procedures that are within the authorized scope of practice of the RN, LPN/VN, or routine functions of the assistive personnel. The description in the question instead matches Brief.
Time scarcity: A feeling of racing against a clock that is continually working against you. The description in the question instead matches Brief.

The inability to voluntarily move muscles.

Kernig sign: Refers to pain that is elicited on passive extension of the client’s knees. The description in the question instead matches Akinesia.
Cholinergic crisis: Respiratory failure resulting from a high dose of cholinesterase inhibitors. The description in the question instead matches Akinesia.
Epidural space: The potential space between the dura mater and vertebrae (spine). The description in the question instead matches Akinesia.

subject: NP5
stem:
Which entry in the reference comparison “Summary of Interventions For Selected Bladder and Bowel Alterations” matches this information?

Interventions: Maintain strict NPO status; Monitor for return of bowel sounds or change in bowel sounds and report to provider as appropriate; Assess abdomen for distention, rigidity, pain, or worsening of symptoms and report to provider as appropriate; Insert and/or maintain nasogastric tube as ordered

options.rationale: Constipation: Implement bowel regimen as ordered, such as oral stool softeners, mild stimulant laxatives, progressing to stronger laxatives, rectal suppositories, or enemas; Provide client education and encouragement regarding the importance of: Increased oral fluids to help soften stool Increased dietary fiber to bulk up stool Increased activity to promote peristalsis; Increased oral fluids to help soften stool; Increased dietary fiber to bulk up stool; Increased activity to promote peristalsis. The description in the question instead matches Intestinal Obstruction or Paralytic Ileus.

Fecal Impaction: Administer mineral oil enemas; Digitally remove impacted stool using a lubricated, gloved finger. The description in the question instead matches Intestinal Obstruction or Paralytic Ileus.

The matching entry is Intestinal Obstruction or Paralytic Ileus. Interventions: Maintain strict NPO status; Monitor for return of bowel sounds or change in bowel sounds and report to provider as appropriate; Assess abdomen for distention, rigidity, pain, or worsening of symptoms and report to provider as appropriate; Insert and/or maintain nasogastric tube as ordered

Diarrhea: Encourage oral fluid intake; Maintain IV hydration as ordered; Monitor for electrolyte disturbances; Monitor for skin breakdown and apply skin protectants as appropriate; Administer medications to slow intestinal motility as ordered and as appropriate; Insert and/or maintain rectal tube as ordered. The description in the question instead matches Intestinal Obstruction or Paralytic Ileus.

rationale: The matching entry is Intestinal Obstruction or Paralytic Ileus. An official way of completing a task.

Communication conflict: Occurs when there is a failure in the exchange of information. The description in the question instead matches Procedure.

Two-challenge rule: A strategy for advocating for client safety that includes a team member assertively voicing their concern at least two times to ensure that it has been heard by the decision-maker. The description in the question instead matches Procedure.

subject: NP5
stem:
In Application Of The Nursing Process To Mental Health Care, which concept matches this description?

The mental action or process of acquiring knowledge and understanding through thought, experience, and the senses. It includes thinking, knowing, remembering, judging, and problem-solving.

options.rationale: Cognition is the matching concept. In this reference context: The mental action or process of acquiring knowledge and understanding through thought, experience, and the senses. It includes thinking, knowing, remembering, judging, and problem-solving.

SMART outcomes: Outcome statements should contain five components easily remembered using the “SMART” mnemonic: Specific, Measurable, Attainable/Action-oriented, Relevant/Realistic, with a Time frame. The description in the question instead matches Cognition.

Magical thinking: A cognitive process in which an individual believes that their thoughts, words, or actions can directly influence events in the physical world in a way that defies the laws of cause and effect. The description in the question instead matches Cognition.

Nursing diagnosis: A clinical judgment concerning a human response to health conditions/life processes or a vulnerability for that response, by an individual, family, group, or community. The description in the question instead matches Cognition.

subject: NP5
stem:
In Stress, Coping, And Crisis Intervention, which concept matches this description?

A type of developmental crisis that occurs during normal life transitions or stages of growth.

options.rationale: Maturational crisis is the matching concept. In this reference context: A type of developmental crisis that occurs during normal life transitions or stages of growth.

Defense mechanisms: Unconscious reaction patterns used by individuals to protect themselves from anxiety that arises from stress and conflict. The description in the question instead matches Maturational crisis.

Problem-focused coping: Adaptive coping strategies that typically focus on seeking treatment such as counseling or cognitive behavioral therapy. The description in the question instead matches Maturational crisis.

Psychological aggression: The use of verbal and/or nonverbal communication with the intent to harm another partner mentally or emotionally and/or to exert control over another partner. The description in the question instead matches Maturational crisis.

stem:
Which entry in the reference comparison “Common Chronic Conditions of the Urinary System and Related Interventions” matches this information?

Symptoms to Report: Increased pain in the abdomen or pain with voiding.

options.rationale: Urinary Incontinence: Change in the frequency or amount of incontinence. The description in the question instead matches Kidney Stones.
The matching entry is Kidney Stones. Symptoms to Report: Increased pain in the abdomen or pain with voiding.

Urinary Tract Infection: Increased frequency of voiding; pain, itching, or burning with voiding; voiding in small amounts; strong odor; dark or cloudy urine; and/or sediment or blood in the urine. A sudden increase in confusion can also indicate infection. The description in the question instead matches Kidney Stones.

Chronic Kidney Failure: Puffiness around the eyes, frequent urge to urinate, urination in increasingly smaller amounts, dry and itchy skin, and/or fatigue. The description in the question instead matches Kidney Stones.

Surgery that involves the replacement of a failed organ or tissue with a healthy organ or tissue from a donor.

options.rationale: Diagnostic surgery: Surgery performed to obtain a definitive diagnosis or to assess the extent of a disease or condition. The description in the question instead matches Transplantation surgery.

Palliative surgery: Surgery performed to alleviate symptoms, reduce pain, or improve the client’s comfort without curing the disease. The description in the question instead matches Transplantation surgery.

Formerly called Mongolian spots; these are bluish skin discolorations found in newborns, more common in African American, Native American, and Hispanic infants. They usually fade by age four.

Atrial Fibrillation: Characterized by atrial quivering that can cause decreased cardiac output because the ventricles are not able to fill and pump the appropriate amount of blood with each beat. The description in the question instead matches First-Degree Heart Block.

Ventricular Fibrillation: Characterized by quivering ventricles with no effective contractions and no cardiac output. This is the most dangerous arrhythmia because of lack of cardiac output and requires immediate initiation of CPR and emergency response. The description in the question instead matches First-Degree Heart Block.

subject: NP4
stem:
In Digestive System Terminology, which concept matches this description?

Dry mouth, often due to a decrease in saliva production.

options.rationale: Bowel retraining: Involves teaching the body to have a bowel movement at a certain time of the day. The description in the question instead matches Xerostomia.
Stool softeners: Laxatives that facilitate movement of water and fats into stool to make it soft and improve regularity of bowel movements. The description in the question instead matches Xerostomia.
Xerostomia is the matching concept. In this reference context: Dry mouth, often due to a decrease in saliva production.
Digestion: The process by which food is broken down into absorbable units. The description in the question instead matches Xerostomia.

rationale: Xerostomia is the matching concept. In this reference context: Dry mouth, often due to a decrease in saliva production.

subject: NP2
stem:
In Reproductive Concepts, which concept matches this description?

Sexual drive or desire, influenced by biological, psychological, and social factors.

options.rationale: Genital herpes: A viral STI caused by the herpes simplex virus (HSV). It results in painful sores or blisters on the genitals, rectum, or mouth. There is no cure, but antiviral medications can reduce symptoms and transmission. The description in the question instead matches Libido.
Etonogestrel implant: A tiny, thin rod about the size of a matchstick that is inserted into a woman’s arm by a health care provider. The description in the question instead matches Libido.
Testosterone: The primary male sex hormone responsible for the development of male secondary sex characteristics and reproductive functions. The description in the question instead matches Libido.
Libido is the matching concept. In this reference context: Sexual drive or desire, influenced by biological, psychological, and social factors.

subject: NP5
stem:
In Depressive Disorders, which concept matches this description?

A chronic form of depression that is typically less severe in intensity than major depressive disorder but lasts much longer.

options.rationale: Prolonged grief disorder: A disorder that is characterized by intense longing and preoccupation with the deceased person that persists beyond 12 months and causes significant impairment. The description in the question instead matches Persistent depressive disorder.

Persistent depressive disorder is the matching concept. In this reference context: A chronic form of depression that is typically less severe in intensity than major depressive disorder but lasts much longer.

Rhabdomyolysis: Severe muscle breakdown that releases myoglobin into the bloodstream and subsequently clogging renal filtrations and causing kidney damage. The description in the question instead matches Persistent depressive disorder.

Premenstrual dysphoric disorder: A severe and disabling form of premenstrual syndrome (PMS) that involves significant mood disturbances and physical symptoms occurring in the week or two before menstruation. The description in the question instead matches Persistent depressive disorder.

rationale: Persistent depressive disorder is the matching concept. In this reference context: A chronic form of depression that is typically less severe in intensity than major depressive disorder but lasts much longer.

subject: CROSS
stem:
In Autonomic Nervous System, which concept matches this description?

Postganglionic neuron where acetylcholine (ACh) is released that stimulates nicotinic receptors and muscarinic receptors. Also relating to drugs that inhibit, enhance, or mimic the action of ACh.

options.rationale: Parasympathetic nervous system: Includes nerves outside the brain and spinal cord. Associated with the “rest and digest” response. Stimulation of PNS causes decreased heart rate, decreased blood pressure via vasodilation, bronchial constriction, and stimulates intestinal motility, salivation, and relaxation of the bladder. The description in the question instead matches Cholinergic.

Adrenergic: Postganglionic neuron where neurotransmitters norepinephrine and epinephrine are released. Includes alpha (α)-receptors and beta (β)-receptors. The description in the question instead matches Cholinergic.

Cholinergic is the matching concept. In this reference context: Postganglionic neuron where acetylcholine (ACh) is released that stimulates nicotinic receptors and muscarinic receptors. Also relating to drugs that inhibit, enhance, or mimic the action of ACh.
Autonomic nervous system: Controls cardiac and smooth muscle, as well as glandular tissue; associated with involuntary responses. The description in the question instead matches Cholinergic.

rationale: Cholinergic is the matching concept. In this reference context: Postganglionic neuron where acetylcholine (ACh) is released that stimulates nicotinic receptors and muscarinic receptors. Also relating to drugs that inhibit, enhance, or mimic the action of ACh.

Deficiency: Fatigue, memory deficits, insomnia, chest pain, abdominal pain, anorexia, numbness of extremities, muscle wasting, heart failure, and shock in severe cases.

options.rationale: B3: Pellagra characterized by skin lesions at pressure points/sun exposed skin, glossitis (swollen tongue), constipation progressing to bloody diarrhea, abdominal pain, abdominal distention, nausea, psychosis, and encephalopathy. The description in the question instead matches B1.

B12: Pernicious anemia from lack of intrinsic factor in intestines. Early Signs: weight loss, abdominal pain, peripheral neuropathy, weakness, hyporeflexia, and ataxia. Late Signs: irritability, depression, paranoia, and confusion. The description in the question instead matches B1.

B6: Rare due to presence in most foods. Peripheral neuropathy, seizures refractory to antiseizure medications, anemia, glossitis (swollen tongue), seborrheic dermatitis, depression, and confusion. The description in the question instead matches B1.
The matching entry is B1. Deficiency: Fatigue, memory deficits, insomnia, chest pain, abdominal pain, anorexia, numbness of extremities, muscle wasting, heart failure, and shock in severe cases.

subject: CROSS
stem:
In Facilitation of Elimination, which concept matches this description?

A catheter used for intermittent urinary catheterization; it does not have a balloon at the insertion end.

options.rationale: Straight catheter is the matching concept. In this reference context: A catheter used for intermittent urinary catheterization; it does not have a balloon at the insertion end.
Urostomy: The ureters (tubes that carry urine from the kidney to the bladder) are attached to a stoma to bypass the bladder. The description in the question instead matches Straight catheter.

Coude catheter: A catheter specifically designed to maneuver around obstructions or blockages in the urethra such as with enlarged prostate glands in males. Coude originates from the French word that means “bend.”. The description in the question instead matches Straight catheter.
Skin tears: Wounds caused by mechanical forces, typically in the nonelastic skin of older adults. The description in the question instead matches Straight catheter.

subject: NP4
stem:
Which entry in the reference comparison “Non-Insulin Antidiabetic Medications” matches this information?

Mechanism of Action: Act on the kidneys to reduce the reabsorption of glucose and promote urinary glucose excretion.

options.rationale: The matching entry is Sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 SLT-2 inhibitors. Mechanism of Action: Act on the kidneys to reduce the reabsorption of glucose and promote urinary glucose excretion.
Thiazolidinediones: Increase cellular insulin sensitivity and cellular uptake of glucose. The description in the question instead matches Sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 SLT-2 inhibitors.

Sulfonylureas: Stimulate the pancreas to release more insulin when there is still some insulin production by the pancreas. The description in the question instead matches Sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 SLT-2 inhibitors.

Dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors: Block the DPP-4 enzyme that inactivates incretin hormones, thus increasing the level of incretin. Incretins stimulate the release of insulin and reduce the production of glucagon. The description in the question instead matches Sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 SLT-2 inhibitors.

rationale: The matching entry is Sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 SLT-2 inhibitors. Mechanism of Action: Act on the kidneys to reduce the reabsorption of glucose and promote urinary glucose excretion.

stem:
In High-Risk Perinatal Client Care, which concept matches this description?

A surgical procedure to remove one or both Fallopian tubes; often performed to treat ectopic pregnancy or prevent future complications.

options.rationale: Salpingectomy is the matching concept. In this reference context: A surgical procedure to remove one or both Fallopian tubes; often performed to treat ectopic pregnancy or prevent future complications.

One-hour oral glucose tolerance test: A screening test for gestational diabetes involving the measurement of blood sugar one hour after consuming a glucose drink. The description in the question instead matches Salpingectomy.

Fundal massage: A procedure of applying firm pressure to the fundus to induce a uterine contraction and to stop the blood from pumping out of the spiral arteries. The goal is to cause the uterus to contract into the size of a small, hard ball. The description in the question instead matches Salpingectomy.
Cervical dilation and curettage: A surgical procedure to remove tissue from the uterus; often performed after miscarriage or abortion. The description in the question instead matches Salpingectomy.

subject: CROSS
stem:
Which entry in the reference comparison “Summary of Safe Medication Administration Guidelines” matches this information?

Additional Information: Check all medications’ expiration dates before administering them. Medications can become inactive after their expiration date.

options.text: Perform appropriate patient assessments before medication administration
options.rationale: Perform appropriate patient assessments before medication administration: Assess the patient prior to administering medications to ensure the patient is receiving the correct medication, for the correct reason, and at the correct time. For example, a nurse reviews lab values and performs a cardiac assessment prior to administering cardiac medication. See more information regarding specific patient assessments during parenteral medication administration in the “Applying the Nursing Process” section. The description in the question instead matches Ensure medication has not expired.

The matching entry is Ensure medication has not expired. Additional Information: Check all medications’ expiration dates before administering them. Medications can become inactive after their expiration date.

options.text: Be diligent and perform medication calculations accurately
options.rationale: Be diligent and perform medication calculations accurately: Double-check and verify medication calculations. Incorrect calculation of medication dosages causes medication errors that can compromise patient safety. The description in the question instead matches Ensure medication has not expired.

options.text: Communicate with the patient before and after administration
options.rationale: Communicate with the patient before and after administration: Provide information to the patient about the medication before administering it. Answer their questions regarding usage, dose, and special considerations. Give the patient an opportunity to ask questions and include family members if appropriate. The description in the question instead matches Ensure medication has not expired.

rationale: The matching entry is Ensure medication has not expired. Additional Information: Check all medications’ expiration dates before administering them. Medications can become inactive after their expiration date.

options.rationale: Rh sensitization: Occurs when a pregnant woman with Rh-negative blood is exposed to Rh-positive blood, causing her immune system to produce antibodies to attack the Rh-positive blood. The description in the question instead matches Amniotic fluid index.

Maternal mortality rate: Death while pregnant or within 42 days of the end of pregnancy, irrespective of the duration and site of the pregnancy, from any cause related to or aggravated by the pregnancy or its management, but not from accidental or incidental causes. The description in the question instead matches Amniotic fluid index.
Amniotic fluid index is the matching concept. In this reference context: A standardized way to assess the sufficiency of the amniotic fluid quantity in pregnancy and is obtained via ultrasound.

Naegele’s Rule: A three-step calculation based on a 28-day menstrual cycle used to determine a pregnant woman’s due date. To calculate, subtract three months from the first day of the client’s last menstrual period and then add seven days and then adjust the year. The description in the question instead matches Amniotic fluid index.

Nursing Considerations and Side Effects: Initial side effects of levodopa-carbidopa may include nausea, low blood pressure, restlessness, and drowsiness.; Side effects of long-term or extended use of levodopa may include hallucinations, psychosis, and dyskinesia.

options.text: Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitors Fluoxetine Hydrochloride
options.rationale: Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitors Fluoxetine Hydrochloride: Effective for treating depression but may aggravate symptoms of Parkinson’s disease. The description in the question instead matches Antiparkinson’s AgentCarbidopa/Levodopa.

options.text: Monoamine Oxidase Inhibitors SelegilineRasagilineZydis Selegiline HCL
options.rationale: Monoamine Oxidase Inhibitors SelegilineRasagilineZydis Selegiline HCL: Used in combination with a dopamine agonist to postpone the initiation of carbidopa or levodopa therapy. Adverse effects are similar to that of levodopa.; Teach clients taking MAOIs to avoid foods, beverages, and drugs that contain tyramine, such as cheese; aged, smoked, or cured foods; and not to drink beer or red wine to prevent headache and life-threatening hypertension. If the drug is discontinued, follow restrictions for 14 days after the last dose. The description in the question instead matches Antiparkinson’s AgentCarbidopa/Levodopa.

May be able to hear “gurgling” sounds from the catheter. If the catheter tip has advanced into the heart, cardiac dysrhythmias may occur.

options.rationale: Infection: Assess the catheter insertion site and surrounding area for redness, edema, drainage, and tenderness. Monitor pertinent laboratory results (e.g., WBC). The description in the question instead matches Catheter migration.

Catheter damage or breakage: Assess the site every shift and with flushing. Observe for leaks, tears, pinholes, or drainage after flushing. The description in the question instead matches Catheter migration.

subject: NP2
stem:
In Congenital Heart Defects, which concept matches this description?

A normal shunt during fetal circulation that causes oxygenated blood from the placenta to bypass the fetal liver and move directly into the inferior vena cava.

options.rationale: Ductus venosus is the matching concept. In this reference context: A normal shunt during fetal circulation that causes oxygenated blood from the placenta to bypass the fetal liver and move directly into the inferior vena cava.

Cardiopulmonary bypass: A medical device that routes a client’s blood around the heart and lungs and oxygenates it. Cannulas (special large tubes) are placed into the vena cava where oxygen-poor blood from the body moves into the bypass machine and is oxygenated. From the bypass machine, the oxygenated blood is moved through a cannula into the aorta, where it is pushed out to the body. The description in the question instead matches Ductus venosus.

Hypoplastic left heart syndrome: A congenital heart defect characterized by underdevelopment of the left side of the heart, including the left ventricle, left atrium, mitral valve, and aortic valve. The description in the question instead matches Ductus venosus.
Positive inotropic effect: Improvement in cardiac output by increased contractility (force of the cardiac contraction). The description in the question instead matches Ductus venosus.

rationale: Ductus venosus is the matching concept. In this reference context: A normal shunt during fetal circulation that causes oxygenated blood from the placenta to bypass the fetal liver and move directly into the inferior vena cava.

subject: NP4
stem:
Which entry in the reference comparison “Common Diagnostic Tests for Nervous System Disorders” matches this information?

Description and Indication: Records the muscle and nerve integration and electrical activity. Needle electrodes are inserted into the specific muscle units being tested. Normal, relaxed muscles show no electrical activity, and contracted muscles show electrical activity. The test is indicated for testing for muscle and nerve diseases.

options.rationale: Magnetic resonance imaging: Provides imaging of the brain and spinal cord by using magnetic energy to detect strokes, multiple sclerosis, tumors, trauma, seizures, and brain herniation. Produces greater detail than CT with improved detail of intracranial structures, but the procedure takes longer to complete and may not be appropriate if a client is experiencing a life- threatening emergency.; Contrast agents, such as gadolinium, can be used with MRI to enhance visualization. The description in the question instead matches Electromyography.

Electroencephalography: Electrodes are placed on the scalp to record electrical activity of the cerebral hemispheres. Each graphic recording represents electrical impulses within the brain. The frequency, amplitude, and characteristics of the brain waves are recorded to evaluate seizure disorders, cerebral disease, brain injury, and brain death. The description in the question instead matches Electromyography.

The matching entry is Electromyography. Description and Indication: Records the muscle and nerve integration and electrical activity. Needle electrodes are inserted into the specific muscle units being tested. Normal, relaxed muscles show no electrical activity, and contracted muscles show electrical activity. The test is indicated for testing for muscle and nerve diseases.

Positron emission tomography: Measures metabolic activity of the brain to determine cell death or damage. A radioactive isotope is injected that shows up as a bright spot on the image if abnormal activity is occurring. Indicated for clients with stroke, Alzheimer’s disease, seizure disorders, Parkinson’s disease, infection, and tumors. The description in the question instead matches Electromyography.

rationale: The matching entry is Electromyography. Description and Indication: Records the muscle and nerve integration and electrical activity. Needle electrodes are inserted into the specific muscle units being tested. Normal, relaxed muscles show no electrical activity, and contracted muscles show electrical activity. The test is indicated for testing for muscle and nerve diseases.

In Cardiovascular System Terminology, which concept matches this description?

The number of heartbeats per minute, with normal resting HR for an adult being 60–100 bpm.

options.rationale: Heart rate is the matching concept. In this reference context: The number of heartbeats per minute, with normal resting HR for an adult being 60–100 bpm.

Atherosclerosis: Hardening and narrowing of arteries due to the buildup of cholesterol and other fats, known as plaque, within the lining of the arteries. The description in the question instead matches Heart rate.

Pulse: The rhythmic expansion and recoil of arteries resulting from heart contraction; can be felt over arteries close to the body’s surface. The description in the question instead matches Heart rate.
Varicose veins: Enlarged, swollen, and twisting veins, often appearing blue or dark purple as a result of faulty valves in the veins. The description in the question instead matches Heart rate.

rationale: Heart rate is the matching concept. In this reference context: The number of heartbeats per minute, with normal resting HR for an adult being 60–100 bpm.

stem:

Additional Information: Use a needleless system and engineered safety devices for prevention of needlestick injuries when preparing injectable medications whenever possible.

options.text: Participate in required training and education
options.rationale: Participate in required training and education: Attend training on injury-prevention strategies related to needles and safety devices per agency policy. The description in the question instead matches Reduce or eliminate all hazards related to needles.

The description in the question instead matches Reduce or eliminate all hazards related to needles.

subject: NP4
stem:
In Mobility, which concept matches this description?

The ability of a person to move around in their environment, including walking, standing up from a chair, sitting down from standing, and moving around in bed.

options.rationale: Fowler’s positioning: A position where the client is supine with the head of bed placed at a 45- to 90-degree angle. The bed can be used to slightly flex the hips to help prevent the client from migrating downwards in bed. The description in the question instead matches Functional mobility.

options.text: Timed Get Up and Go Test
options.rationale: Timed Get Up and Go Test: A mobility assessment by nurses that begins by having the client stand up from an armchair, walk three yards, turn, walk back to the chair, and sit down. As the client performs these maneuvers, their posture, alignment, balance, and gait are analyzed as the client’s mobility status is assessed. The description in the question instead matches Functional mobility.

Functional mobility is the matching concept. In this reference context: The ability of a person to move around in their environment, including walking, standing up from a chair, sitting down from standing, and moving around in bed.

Tripod position: A position where the client sits in a chair with their elbows on their knees or at the side of the bed with their arms resting on an overbed table. This position is often naturally assumed by clients with breathing difficulties. The description in the question instead matches Functional mobility.

rationale: Functional mobility is the matching concept. In this reference context: The ability of a person to move around in their environment, including walking, standing up from a chair, sitting down from standing, and moving around in bed.
keyPoint: Functional mobility: The ability of a person to move around in their environment, including walking, standing up from a chair, sitting down from standing, and moving around in bed.

In Sensory System Terminology, which concept matches this description?

A defined level of visual impairment that has been established as a threshold for eligibility for governmental disability benefits; typically, visual acuity of 20/200 or less in the best-corrected eye.

options.rationale: Legal blindness is the matching concept. In this reference context: A defined level of visual impairment that has been established as a threshold for eligibility for governmental disability benefits; typically, visual acuity of 20/200 or less in the best-corrected eye.
Pupil: The hole at the center of the eye that allows light to enter, its size is controlled by the iris. The description in the question instead matches Legal blindness.

Conductive hearing loss: Hearing loss caused by problems with the ear canal, eardrum, or middle ear and its little bones (the malleus, incus, and stapes). The description in the question instead matches Legal blindness.
Pinna: Another term for the auricle, the visible part of the ear that resides outside of the head. The description in the question instead matches Legal blindness.

stem:
Which entry in the reference comparison “Common Defense Mechanisms” matches this information?

Examples: A child who was toilet trained reverts to wetting their pants after their parents’ divorce.

options.rationale: Splitting: A client tells the nurse they are the most wonderful person in the world, but after the nurse enforces the unit rules with them, the client tells the nurse they are the worst person they have ever met. The description in the question instead matches Regression.
The matching entry is Regression. Examples: A child who was toilet trained reverts to wetting their pants after their parents’ divorce.
Reaction Formation: A client who hates their mother writes in their journal that their mom is a wonderful mother. The description in the question instead matches Regression.

Sublimation: An individual with an exhibitionistic impulse channels this impulse into creating dance choreography. A person with a voyeuristic urge completes scientific research and observes research subjects. An individual with an aggressive drive joins the football team. The description in the question instead matches Regression.

rationale: The matching entry is Regression. Examples: A child who was toilet trained reverts to wetting their pants after their parents’ divorce.

Promotes growth in children, helps maintain normal body structure in adults, and plays a role in metabolism in both children and adults.

options.rationale: Aldosterone: A mineralocorticoid hormone produced by the adrenal gland that regulates the salt and water balance of the body in the kidneys by increasing the retention of sodium and water and excreting potassium. The description in the question instead matches Growth hormone.

Posterior pituitary gland: Gland which secretes two hormones produced by the hypothalamus called oxytocin and antidiuretic hormone (ADH). The description in the question instead matches Growth hormone.

Identification: Wide bizarre QRS complexes within a normal underlying rhythm.; May be single or multiple PVCs.

options.rationale: The matching entry is Premature Ventricular Contraction [ ]. Identification: Wide bizarre QRS complexes within a normal underlying rhythm.; May be single or multiple PVCs.
Asystole[ ]: A flat line appears on the ECG.; There is no impulse occurring, so nothing is measurable. The description in the question instead matches Premature Ventricular Contraction [ ].
Pulseless Electrical Activity [ ]: ECG components may be present, but the client does not have a pulse. The description in the question instead matches Premature Ventricular Contraction [ ].

Ventricular Fibrillation [ ]: Nothing can be measured because there is just a fibrillatory line.; Can be coarse or fine fibrillatory waves. Coarse waves are taller than fine. Fine V-fib is harder to treat and convert to a sustaining rhythm. The description in the question instead matches Premature Ventricular Contraction [ ].

options.rationale: Magnetic Resonance Imaging: Imaging obtained by placing the infant or child in a machine that emits a strong magnetic field that surrounds the body. Holter Monitor: A portable ECG device that the client wears that records electrical activity of the heart over a period of time, usually 24-48 hours, on an outpatient basis. The client or parent presses a button to record events such as shortness of breath or palpitations. The recording shows arrhythmias and any other normal or abnormal electrical activity that occurs during these recorded events. The description in the question instead matches Chest X-ray.

options.rationale: Sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 SLT-2 inhibitors: Act on the kidneys to reduce the reabsorption of glucose and promote urinary glucose excretion. The description in the question instead matches Thiazolidinediones.

Rationale: A portable ECG device that the client wears that records electrical activity of the heart over a period of time, usually 24-48 hours, on an outpatient basis. The client or parent presses a button to record events such as shortness of breath or palpitations. The recording shows arrhythmias and any other normal or abnormal electrical activity that occurs during these recorded events.

options.rationale: Ventilation-Perfusion Scan: Involves inhalation of a radioactive gas to examine the airways, followed by injection of an isotope intravenously, which is then scanned and tracked to determine blood flow and flow patterns through the lung vessels. The description in the question instead matches Holter Monitor.

Electrocardiogram: Provides a reading of electrical activity of the heart through electrodes placed across the chest. Shows heart rate, rhythm, arrhythmias, and any other normal or abnormal electrical activity. The description in the question instead matches Holter Monitor.

Structures within the kidneys responsible for filtering waste and excess fluids from the blood to produce urine.

Any form of treatment for mental health disorders that attempts to alter physiological functioning, including drug therapies, electroconvulsive therapy, and psychosurgery.

subject: NP5
stem:
In Substance Use Disorders, which concept matches this description?

A rapid-onset, fluctuating disturbance of attention and cognition, sometimes associated with hallucinations, due to alcohol withdrawal. In its most severe manifestation, DTs are accompanied by agitation and signs of extreme autonomic hyperactivity, including fever, severe tachycardia, hypertension, and drenching sweats. DTs typically begin between 72 and 96 hours after the client’s last drink.

options.rationale: Binge drinking: Consuming several standard drinks on one occasion in the past 30 days, defined for males as drinking five or more standard alcoholic drinks on one occasion, and for females as drinking four or more standard drinks on one occasion. The description in the question instead matches Delirium tremens.

Substance use disorder: A chronic illness caused by repeated misuse of psychoactive substances (e.g., alcohol, caffeine, cannabis, hallucinogens, inhalants, opioids, sedatives, hypnotics, anxiolytics, stimulants, and tobacco) that have a common effect of directly activating the brain’s reward system. The description in the question instead matches Delirium tremens.
Protective factors: Factors that help prevent substance use disorders from developing despite the risk factors that are present. The description in the question instead matches Delirium tremens.

Delirium tremens is the matching concept. DTs typically begin between 72 and 96 hours after the client’s last drink.

options.text: Timed Get Up and Go Test
options.rationale: Timed Get Up and Go Test: A mobility assessment by nurses that begins by having the client stand up from an armchair, walk three yards, turn, walk back to the chair, and sit down. The description in the question instead matches Lateral positioning.

Trendelenburg positioning: A position where the head of the bed is placed lower than the client’s feet. An abnormally low number of circulating white blood cells (WBC).

options.rationale: Coagulation cascade: A complex series of reactions involving a variety of coagulation factors that eventually leads to the formation of a fibrin clot. The description in the question instead matches Leukopenia.

Anemia: A clinical sign characterized by a reduction in either the number of red blood cells, the amount of hemoglobin, or the hematocrit (percentage of red blood cells in the total blood volume). The description in the question instead matches Leukopenia.
Pulsatile tinnitus: Rhythmic pulsing sound in the ear. The description in the question instead matches Leukopenia.
Leukopenia is the matching concept. In this reference context: An abnormally low number of circulating white blood cells (WBC).

Mnemonic for introducing oneself in health care that includes Acknowledge, Introduce, Duration, Explanation, and Thank You.

General survey assessment: A component of a patient assessment that observes the entire patient as a whole. Methods or devices used to prevent pregnancy. These can include hormonal, barrier, surgical, or behavioral techniques.

Small particles are injected into the uterine arteries during this procedure to cut off blood flow to the fibroid. The description in the question instead matches Contraception.

Breast ultrasound: A medical imaging technique that uses sound waves to create images of the breast tissue. It is often used to further evaluate abnormalities found on a mammogram. The description in the question instead matches Contraception.

In Leadership Principles, which concept matches this description?

Immediate availability to continually coordinate, direct, and inspect at first hand the practice of another.

options.rationale: Direct supervision is the matching concept. In this reference context: Immediate availability to continually coordinate, direct, and inspect at first hand the practice of another.

Acute versus chronic conditions: A prioritization strategy that considers acute versus chronic medical conditions. Acute conditions have a sudden and severe onset. These conditions occur due to a sudden illness or injury, and the body often has a significant response as it attempts to adapt. Chronic conditions have a slow onset and may gradually worsen over time. The description in the question instead matches Direct supervision.

Five rights of delegation: A method to ensure proper and appropriate delegation, including right task, right circumstance, right person, right directions and communication, and right supervision and evaluation. The description in the question instead matches Direct supervision.

Airway, breathing, and circulation: A prioritization strategy, similar to Maslow’s Hierarchy of Needs, that guides nursing decision-making based on the most critical needs for preserving human life. The description in the question instead matches Direct supervision.

stem:
Which entry in the reference comparison “Examples of Modern Family Structures” matches this information?

Description: Parents have different religious, faith, or spirituality beliefs. They may choose to raise their children according to one religious/faith/spirituality belief or both.

options.rationale: Adoptive families: Adoptive parents legally take a child into their family and raise them as their own because of infertility issues or because they prefer adoption. Adoption may be open or closed. Open adoption ranges from simply knowing the identities of the birth parent(s) to having a continued relationship with the birth parents as the child grows up. Closed adoption means the family does not have access to information about the birth parent(s) nor do birth parents have access to information about the adoptive family or child. The description in the question instead matches Families with multi-religious/faith/spirituality beliefs.

Transgender parents: A transgender parent is a parent who identifies as a different gender from their biological gender. A transgender parent may transition to a different gender prior to or after having a child.; View a supplementary Vimeo video on care considerations for children of LGBTQIA families: Considerations for Children of LGBTQIA+ Families. The description in the question instead matches Families with multi-religious/faith/spirituality beliefs.

Teen parents: Teens raising their children may elect to do so as a single parent, with a partner, or with the help of their families. Teens who become pregnant while still in high school may participate in supportive programs where they can return to school and have access to parenting classes and childcare. The description in the question instead matches Families with multi-religious/faith/spirituality beliefs.

The matching entry is Families with multi-religious/faith/spirituality beliefs. Description: Parents have different religious, faith, or spirituality beliefs. They may choose to raise their children according to one religious/faith/spirituality belief or both.

options.rationale: Placenta previa is the matching concept. In this reference context: A condition where the placenta partially or completely covers the cervix, increasing the risk of bleeding during pregnancy and delivery.
Uterine subinvolution: The delayed return of the uterus to its normal size and condition after childbirth. The description in the question instead matches Placenta previa.

In Lymphatic & Immune Systems Terminology, which concept matches this description?

Programmed cell death that is disrupted in some cancers, allowing malignant cells to avoid natural cell death and continue uncontrolled growth.

options.rationale: Apoptosis is the matching concept. In this reference context: Programmed cell death that is disrupted in some cancers, allowing malignant cells to avoid natural cell death and continue uncontrolled growth.

Lymphatic system: A network of organs, lymph nodes, lymph ducts, and lymph vessels that produce and transport lymph from tissue spaces to the bloodstream and is a major part of the body’s immune system. The description in the question instead matches Apoptosis.

Spleen: An organ in the upper far left part of the abdomen, to the left of the stomach, which filters blood and is involved in immune response. The description in the question instead matches Apoptosis.
Lymphocyte: A type of white blood cell in the vertebrate immune system. The description in the question instead matches Apoptosis.

rationale: Apoptosis is the matching concept. In this reference context: Programmed cell death that is disrupted in some cancers, allowing malignant cells to avoid natural cell death and continue uncontrolled growth.

subject: NP2
stem:
In Labor & Delivery Care, which concept matches this description?

Refers to the presence of extension of the fetal head and neck.

options.rationale: Breech presentation: Position in which the fetal buttocks (or legs) enter the pelvis first. The description in the question instead matches Fetal attitude.
Fetal attitude is the matching concept. In this reference context: Refers to the presence of extension of the fetal head and neck.

Vertex presentation: The most common type of cephalic presentation, meaning the fetal head is down in the maternal pelvis with its neck flexed and the chin tucked into its chest, thus minimizing the diameter of the fetal head to conform to the maternal pelvis. The description in the question instead matches Fetal attitude.
Right occiput anterior: Position in which the occiput slightly facing the mother’s right side. The description in the question instead matches Fetal attitude.

A complication associated with preeclampsia that can cause life-threatening bleeding issues during labor and postpartum evidenced by hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes, and low platelet count.

Smudging: Burning sacred herbs to cleanse, purify, and connect with the spirit world. The description in the question instead matches HELLP syndrome.

Occiput anterior: Position in which the fetal occiput is close to the maternal symphysis pubis, and the face is pointed towards the mother’s spine. The description in the question instead matches HELLP syndrome.
Intrauterine resuscitation: Interventions to help restore fetal blood flow and oxygenation. The description in the question instead matches HELLP syndrome.

stem:
In Obstetrics Terminology, which concept matches this description?

The birth of a fetus that has died in the uterus, typically after surviving at least the first 28 weeks of pregnancy.

Fetal heart monitoring: Tracking the fetal heart rate during pregnancy and labor. The description in the question instead matches Stillborn.
Premature preterm rupture of membranes: Rupture of the amniotic sac before 37 weeks of pregnancy. The description in the question instead matches Stillborn.

Unexpected Finding (Dysfunction): Gag reflex is not present; patient has dysphagia.

Lay people who are trained to provide emotional, physical, and social support during pregnancy, labor, and postpartum.

subject: NP3
stem:
In IV Therapy Management, which concept matches this description?

A condition when there is too much fluid in the blood. Patients may present with shortness of breath, edema to the extremities, and weight gain.

options.rationale: Hypovolemia: A decrease in the volume of blood plasma, which can be a critical condition following postpartum hemorrhage. The description in the question instead matches Fluid volume overload.

Hypovolemic shock: A life-threatening condition caused by severe blood or fluid loss, leading to inadequate oxygen delivery to tissues and organs. The description in the question instead matches Fluid volume overload.
Third spacing: Abnormal accumulation of fluid within interstitial spaces causing swelling within tissues. The description in the question instead matches Fluid volume overload.

subject: CROSS
stem:
In Grief And Loss, which concept matches this description?

A legal document that identifies a trusted individual to serve as a decision maker for health issues when the client is no longer able to speak for themselves.

options.rationale: Health care power of attorney is the matching concept. In this reference context: A legal document that identifies a trusted individual to serve as a decision maker for health issues when the client is no longer able to speak for themselves.
Anorexia: Loss of appetite or loss of desire to eat. The description in the question instead matches Health care power of attorney.

Cardiopulmonary resuscitation: Emergency treatment initiated when a client’s breathing stops or their heart stops beating. It may involve chest compressions and mouth-to-mouth breathing, electric shocks to stop lethal cardiac rhythms, breathing tubes to open the airway, or cardiac medications. The description in the question instead matches Health care power of attorney.

Comfort care: Care that occurs when the client’s and medical team’s goals shift from curative interventions to symptom control, pain relief, and quality of life. The description in the question instead matches Health care power of attorney.

rationale: Health care power of attorney is the matching concept. In this reference context: A legal document that identifies a trusted individual to serve as a decision maker for health issues when the client is no longer able to speak for themselves.
