subject: NP4
stem:
In Demonstrate Reporting and Documentation of Client Data, which concept matches this description?

Temperature taken in the rectum. It provides the most accurate temperature measurement but is considered an invasive procedure.

options.rationale: Fecal immunochemical test: Test that uses antibodies to detect blood in the stool. The description in the question instead matches Rectal temperature.
Large bowel resection: Surgical removal of part of the large intestine. The description in the question instead matches Rectal temperature.
Rectal temperature is the matching concept. In this reference context: Temperature taken in the rectum. It provides the most accurate temperature measurement but is considered an invasive procedure.

Tympanic temperature: Temperature taken using a device placed in the ear. It is more accurate than oral or axillary measurement because the tympanic membrane in the ear shares the same artery that perfuses the hypothalamus (the part of the brain that regulates the body’s temperature). The description in the question instead matches Rectal temperature.

rationale: Rectal temperature is the matching concept. In this reference context: Temperature taken in the rectum. It provides the most accurate temperature measurement but is considered an invasive procedure.

A supervised program that includes exercise training, health education, and breathing techniques for people who have chronic lung conditions.

options.rationale: Pulmonary rehabilitation is the matching concept. In this reference context: A supervised program that includes exercise training, health education, and breathing techniques for people who have chronic lung conditions.

Hilum: The area that connects the lungs to the supporting structures and where the pulmonary vessels enter and exit the lungs. The description in the question instead matches Pulmonary rehabilitation.

Capnography: A sensor that measures the concentration of carbon dioxide exhaled, translated into a waveform and numerical value. The description in the question instead matches Pulmonary rehabilitation.

Bronchial responsiveness testing: Measures the responsiveness of the airway after it has been exposed to an allergen or bronchoconstrictive substance. The description in the question instead matches Pulmonary rehabilitation.

An expansion of the abdomen caused by the accumulation of air or fluid.

Anal canal: A three-inch long section at the end of the gastrointestinal tract that opens to the exterior of the body at the anus. The description in the question instead matches Distention.

An allergic inflammatory condition of the skin, manifesting as dry, itchy patches that resemble a red, flaky rash.

Hospital-acquired MRSA: MRSA infection occurring in people in hospitals or other health care facilities. The description in the question instead matches Eczema.

The backward flow of stomach contents into the esophagus or throat, causing heartburn or acid indigestion.

Probiotics: Live bacteria and yeasts that are good for your health, especially your digestive system. The description in the question instead matches Reflux.

Removal of the uterus using laparoscopic techniques, involving small incisions and a camera.

options.rationale: Total laparoscopic hysterectomy is the matching concept. In this reference context: Removal of the uterus using laparoscopic techniques, involving small incisions and a camera.

Hysterosalpingogram: A common imaging procedure performed to assess for potential causes of infertility in women. During the procedure, radiopaque dye is injected into the uterus and fills the uterine cavity, continues into the fallopian tubes, and eventually reaches fimbriated ends next to the ovaries. Structures are visualized with an x-ray. The description in the question instead matches Total laparoscopic hysterectomy.

Subtotal hysterectomy: Removal of part of the uterus, leaving the cervix in place. The description in the question instead matches Total laparoscopic hysterectomy.

stem:
In Congenital Heart Defects, which concept matches this description?

The amount of pressure the left ventricle must overcome to eject blood out of the heart and to the rest of the body.

options.rationale: Hypercyanotic episode: A severe episode of hypoxia that typically occurs in clients with Tetralogy of Fallot, also known as a “Tet Spell.” During these episodes, there is a significant decrease in blood flow moving to the lungs due to a sudden increase in shunting of blood from the right side to left side of the heart. Deoxygenated blood is pumped out to the body, resulting in signs and symptoms of severe hypoxia. The description in the question instead matches Afterload.
Afterload is the matching concept. In this reference context: The amount of pressure the left ventricle must overcome to eject blood out of the heart and to the rest of the body.
Polycythemia: Elevated number of red blood cells. The description in the question instead matches Afterload.

Obstructive defects: Heart defects that cause a restriction, or obstruction, in blood flow from within the left side of the heart or out through the body. The description in the question instead matches Afterload.

The degree of movement a joint can be moved by a muscle contraction.

Smooth muscle: Involuntary, non-striated muscle that is found in the walls of internal organs such as the stomach, intestine, and blood vessels, controlling their movements. The description in the question instead matches Active range of motion.
Spastic: Relating to or affected by muscle spasm or increased reflexes. The description in the question instead matches Active range of motion.

A body system that regulates extracellular fluids and blood pressure by regulating fluid output and electrolyte excretion.

Hypertonic solution: Intravenous fluids with a higher concentration of dissolved particles than blood plasma. The description in the question instead matches Renin-Angiotensin-Aldosterone System.

A clinical metric that measures the time elapsed between a client’s admission and discharge.

Monitored anesthesia care: The administration of IV sedation and pain management for clients undergoing certain procedures. stem:
Which entry in the reference comparison “Complications/Unexpected Outcomes of CVADs” matches this information?

Assessment: Measure and document the catheter length per agency policy. Assess for dislodgement by identifying any edema at or around the catheter insertion site. Palpate for coiling of the catheter under the skin.

options.rationale: Incorrect placement: Assess for inadequate blood withdrawal, blood flowing back into the tubing, hypotension, cardiac dysrhythmias, and neck vein distension. The description in the question instead matches Dislodgment.

Catheter damage or breakage: Assess the site every shift and with flushing. Observe for leaks, tears, pinholes, or drainage after flushing. The description in the question instead matches Dislodgment.

The matching entry is Dislodgment. Assessment: Measure and document the catheter length per agency policy. Assess for dislodgement by identifying any edema at or around the catheter insertion site. Palpate for coiling of the catheter under the skin.

options.text: Occlusion due to clot formation or malpositioning
options.rationale: Occlusion due to clot formation or malpositioning: Perform recommended site and CVAD system care, including equipment function and checking for blood return and the ability to infuse fluid. Assess for pain and edema at the insertion site (i.e., shoulder, ear, neck, or arm). If an implantable port is in place, assess the noncoring needle for correct placement. The description in the question instead matches Dislodgment.

A congenital condition where the esophagus is malformed, often leading to feeding and swallowing difficulties.

options.rationale: Respiratory distress syndrome: A lung condition in preterm infants caused by surfactant deficiency, leading to difficulty breathing, hypoxia, and respiratory failure. The description in the question instead matches Esophageal atresia.

Necrotizing enterocolitis: A serious intestinal disease in premature infants where portions of the bowel become inflamed, infected, or necrotic, leading to potential perforation and sepsis. The description in the question instead matches Esophageal atresia.

The description in the question instead matches Nutrition and diet.

Chronic health conditions: Preexisting medical conditions are assessed such as diabetes, hypertension, thyroid disorders, and autoimmune diseases because they can impact pregnancy outcomes. The description in the question instead matches Nutrition and diet.

Description: Audible noises with breathing are an indication of respiratory conditions. Further assess lung sounds with a stethoscope for adventitious sounds such as wheezing, rales, or crackles. Secretions can plug the airway, thereby decreasing the amount of oxygen available for gas exchange in the lungs.

options.rationale: Shortness of breath: Dyspnea is a subjective feeling of not getting enough air. Depending on its severity, dyspnea can cause increased levels of anxiety. The description in the question instead matches Noisy breathing.
Restlessness: An early sign of hypoxia resulting in increased movement and the inability to stay still. The description in the question instead matches Noisy breathing.

Secretions can plug the airway, thereby decreasing the amount of oxygen available for gas exchange in the lungs.

Position of client: Clients in respiratory distress often automatically sit up and lean over by resting arms on their legs, referred to as the tripod position. The tripod position enhances lung expansion. Conversely, clients who are hypoxic often feel worse dyspnea when lying flat in bed and avoid the supine position. The description in the question instead matches Noisy breathing.

Which entry in the reference comparison “Pregnancy Risk Factors” matches this information?

Description: Family history of genetic disorders or genetic conditions in the parents are assessed, and genetic counseling and testing are offered before conception.

options.rationale: Emotional and relationship status: Relationship dynamics and stress levels are assessed because of their impact on fertility and emotional well-being. Nurses and health care providers are aware that pregnancy can trigger intimate partner violence (IPV) that can result in injury or death of the mother and/or fetus. Review information in the “Intimate Partner Violence” section of the “Maladaptive Coping Behaviors” chapter. The description in the question instead matches Genetic and family history.

Nutrition and diet: Poor diet and nutritional deficiencies, particularly in folate and other essential nutrients, can impact fertility and increase the risk of birth defects. Low pre-pregnancy maternal weight (BMI< 18.5) is associated with low-birth-weight infants and premature birth, as well as infertility issues. High pre-pregnancy maternal weight (BMI>30) is associated with increased risk for hypertension, prolonged labor, a large-for-gestational-age infant, cesarean birth, wound infections, gestational diabetes, thromboembolic disorders, and postpartum hemorrhage. The description in the question instead matches Genetic and family history.

The matching entry is Genetic and family history. Description: Family history of genetic disorders or genetic conditions in the parents are assessed, and genetic counseling and testing are offered before conception.

Immunization status: Immunity to certain infections such as rubella and varicella is assessed, and vaccinations are updated according to the current CDC vaccination schedule to prevent birth defects. The description in the question instead matches Genetic and family history.

rationale: The matching entry is Genetic and family history. Description: Family history of genetic disorders or genetic conditions in the parents are assessed, and genetic counseling and testing are offered before conception.

subject: CROSS

Summary of Characteristics: • Demonstrates centralized decision-making; • Uses power to control others; • Motivates through fear or reward; • Disregards needs of group members

options.rationale: Resonant: • Builds strong, trusting relationships; • Focuses on the emotions of team members, uses empathy, and manages their own emotions effectively; • Creates a climate of optimism. The description in the question instead matches Authoritarian.

Transformational: • Creates ownership with shared, inspiring vision; • Demonstrates effective communication; • Values relationships; • Considers individuals’ needs and abilities. The description in the question instead matches Authoritarian.

The matching entry is Authoritarian. Summary of Characteristics: • Demonstrates centralized decision-making; • Uses power to control others; • Motivates through fear or reward; • Disregards needs of group members

Transactional: • Allows both parties to receive something for their efforts; • Motivates members with external rewards; • Rewards good performance and penalizes low performance; • Does not focus on team cooperation or commitment to the organization. The description in the question instead matches Authoritarian.

rationale: The matching entry is Authoritarian. Summary of Characteristics: • Demonstrates centralized decision-making; • Uses power to control others; • Motivates through fear or reward; • Disregards needs of group members

stem:
Which entry in the reference comparison “Common Defense Mechanisms” matches this information?

Examples: A person conflicted over expressing anger changes “I hate him” to “He hates me.”

options.rationale: The matching entry is Projection. Examples: A person conflicted over expressing anger changes “I hate him” to “He hates me.”

Sublimation: An individual with an exhibitionistic impulse channels this impulse into creating dance choreography. A person with a voyeuristic urge completes scientific research and observes research subjects. An individual with an aggressive drive joins the football team. The description in the question instead matches Projection.
Regression: A child who was toilet trained reverts to wetting their pants after their parents’ divorce. The description in the question instead matches Projection.
Introjection: A client talks and acts like one of the nurses they admire. The description in the question instead matches Projection.

rationale: The matching entry is Projection. Examples: A person conflicted over expressing anger changes “I hate him” to “He hates me.”

A procedure where a needle biopsy is performed with the guidance of computed tomography (CT) imaging to obtain a tissue sample from the lung or other internal organs.

Chest X-rays: An imaging test that uses small amounts of radiation to produce pictures of the organs, bones, and tissues in the chest area; also called radiographs. The description in the question instead matches CT-guided needle biopsy.
Sputum culture: A test to detect and identify bacteria or fungi that are infecting the lungs or breathing passages. The description in the question instead matches CT-guided needle biopsy.

Defined as smoking one pack of cigarettes a day for a year.

Standard drink: Equivalent to 12 ounces of beer, a 5-ounce glass or wine, or 1.5 ounces of liquor. The description in the question instead matches Pack-year.
Contemplation stage: The client is aware of and acknowledges the risks related to their lifestyle choices and/or behaviors. The description in the question instead matches Pack-year.

Body mass index: The most commonly used assessment of a person’s weight. It is calculated using a formula and the client’s weight and height. The description in the question instead matches Pack-year.

subject: NP5
stem:
In Thought Disorders, which concept matches this description?

A general term used to describe recovery-oriented treatment programs for people with first-episode psychosis, an early stage of schizophrenia.

options.rationale: Tardive dyskinesia: A syndrome of movement disorders that can occur in clients taking first-generation antipsychotics, persisting for at least one month and up to several years despite discontinuation of the medications. The movement disorders include akathisia, dystonia, tics, and other abnormal involuntary movements. The description in the question instead matches Coordinated specialty care.

Coordinated specialty care is the matching concept. In this reference context: A general term used to describe recovery-oriented treatment programs for people with first-episode psychosis, an early stage of schizophrenia.
Catatonia: A pronounced increase or decrease in the rate and amount of movement; excessive movement is purposeless. The description in the question instead matches Coordinated specialty care.

Psychotic episode: An episode of psychosis that can include delusions, hallucinations, disorganized speech, and grossly disorganized or catatonic behavior. The description in the question instead matches Coordinated specialty care.

rationale: Coordinated specialty care is the matching concept. In this reference context: A general term used to describe recovery-oriented treatment programs for people with first-episode psychosis, an early stage of schizophrenia.

stem:
In Communication, which concept matches this description?

A type of documentation where a list of “normal findings” is provided and nurses document assessment findings by confirming normal findings and writing brief documentation notes for any abnormal findings.

options.rationale: Bedside handoff report: A handoff report in hospitals that involves clients, their family members, and both the off-going and the incoming nurses. The report is performed face to face and conducted at the client’s bedside. The description in the question instead matches Charting by exception.

Charting by exception is the matching concept. In this reference context: A type of documentation where a list of “normal findings” is provided and nurses document assessment findings by confirming normal findings and writing brief documentation notes for any abnormal findings.
Nonverbal communication: Facial expressions, tone of voice, pace of the conversation, and body language. The description in the question instead matches Charting by exception.

Receptive aphasia: A type of aphasia where the client has difficulty in understanding what is being communicated to them. The client may be able to verbalize their thoughts and feelings but does not understand what is spoken to them. The description in the question instead matches Charting by exception.

A secondary infection in a client having a preexisting infection. C-diff and yeast infections as a result of antibiotic therapy are examples of superinfections.

Dose dependent: A more significant response occurs in the body when the medication is administered in large doses to provide a large amount of medication to the site of infection for a short period of time. The description in the question instead matches Superinfection.

Methicillin-resistant S. aureus: An infection caused by Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus that is difficult to treat because it exhibits resistance to nearly all available antibiotics. The description in the question instead matches Superinfection.
Pathogen: An organism causing disease to its host. The description in the question instead matches Superinfection.

stem:
In Cognitive Impairments, which concept matches this description?

A type of care selected by clients who are terminally ill and whose health care provider has determined they are expected to live six months or less that focuses on providing comfort and dignity at the end of life. It involves care and support services that can be of great benefit to people in the final stages of dementia and to their families.

options.rationale: Respite care: Care provided at home (by a volunteer or paid service) or in a care setting, such as adult day centers or residential facilities, that allows the caregiver to take a much-needed break. The description in the question instead matches Hospice care.

Sundowning: Increased confusion, anxiety, agitation, pacing, or disorientation in clients with dementia that typically begins at dusk and continues throughout the night. The description in the question instead matches Hospice care.

Adult day care centers: Care that offers people with dementia and other chronic illnesses the opportunity to be social and to participate in activities in a safe environment, while also giving their caregivers the opportunity to work, run errands, or take a much-needed break. The description in the question instead matches Hospice care.

Hospice care is the matching concept. The force of contraction of the heart muscle.

options.rationale: Umbilical vein: A single vessel that originates in the placenta and runs within the umbilical cord, carrying oxygen- and nutrient-rich blood from the mother to the fetus. The description in the question instead matches Contractility.

Patent foramen ovale: An opening between the right and left atria that fails to close at birth when the infant takes its first breaths and pressures within the atria begin to rise. The description in the question instead matches Contractility.

Sarcoplasmic reticulum: The part of the muscle responsible for releasing and storing calcium ions in muscle fibers, causing contraction and relaxation of muscles. The description in the question instead matches Contractility.

Nursing Actions to Support Children in this Stage: Realize that the child or caregiver may refuse a treatment if they feel it will not benefit them or if they feel the risks outweigh the benefits. For example, parents may refuse certain vaccines for their children if they feel their risk of contracting the disease is minimal.

options.rationale: Stage 6: Universal Ethical Principles: Realize that adolescents or parents in this stage may have a vested interest in advancing scientific knowledge. A noninvasive method used during labor to continuously monitor the well-being of the fetus and the progress of uterine contractions.

Consuming several standard drinks on one occasion in the past 30 days, defined for males as drinking five or more standard alcoholic drinks on one occasion, and for females as drinking four or more standard drinks on one occasion.

options.rationale: Protective factors: Factors that help prevent substance use disorders from developing despite the risk factors that are present. The description in the question instead matches Binge drinking.

Substance use disorder: A chronic illness caused by repeated misuse of psychoactive substances (e.g., alcohol, caffeine, cannabis, hallucinogens, inhalants, opioids, sedatives, hypnotics, anxiolytics, stimulants, and tobacco) that have a common effect of directly activating the brain’s reward system. The description in the question instead matches Binge drinking.

Withdrawal management: Interventions that manage the physical and emotional symptoms that occur after a person stops using a psychoactive substance; also referred to as detoxification. Withdrawal symptoms vary in intensity and duration based on the substance(s) used, the duration and amount of use, and the overall health of the individual. The description in the question instead matches Binge drinking.

Binge drinking is the matching concept. In this reference context: Consuming several standard drinks on one occasion in the past 30 days, defined for males as drinking five or more standard alcoholic drinks on one occasion, and for females as drinking four or more standard drinks on one occasion.

Devices that provide a fine mist using oxygen or compressed air to transport the medication from a nebulizer cup into the mouth and into the lungs as the patient breathes normally through a mask or pipe device.

options.rationale: Small-volume nebulizers is the matching concept. In this reference context: Devices that provide a fine mist using oxygen or compressed air to transport the medication from a nebulizer cup into the mouth and into the lungs as the patient breathes normally through a mask or pipe device.
Transdermal route: Patches or disks applied to the skin that deliver medication over an extended period of time. The description in the question instead matches Small-volume nebulizers.

An example of a DPI is tiotropium (Spiriva). The description in the question instead matches Small-volume nebulizers.

Action: Inhibitory effects and helps to control sleep and mood; inhibits pain pathways.

A structured method used to analyze serious adverse events to identify underlying problems that increase the likelihood of errors, while avoiding the trap of focusing on mistakes by individuals.

Never events: Adverse events that are clearly identifiable, measurable, serious (resulting in death or significant disability), and preventable. The description in the question instead matches Root cause analysis.

A type of ovulatory disorder characterized by normal levels of gonadotropins and estrogen but the absence or irregularity of ovulation. This is the most common cause of anovulatory infertility and is often associated with conditions such as polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS).

options.rationale: Normogonadotropic normoestrogenic anovulation is the matching concept. In this reference context: A type of ovulatory disorder characterized by normal levels of gonadotropins and estrogen but the absence or irregularity of ovulation. This is the most common cause of anovulatory infertility and is often associated with conditions such as polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS).

Premenstrual syndrome: A common, cyclical, and multifaceted disorder that occurs during the luteal phase of the menstrual cycle. The description in the question instead matches Normogonadotropic normoestrogenic anovulation.

Nonlactation mastitis: Breast tissue inflammation in a woman who is not breastfeeding, which may or may not be associated with an infection. The description in the question instead matches Normogonadotropic normoestrogenic anovulation.

Endometriosis: A disease in which tissue similar to the lining of the uterus grows outside the uterus, causing inflammation and scar tissue to form in the pelvic region, such as on the ovaries, Fallopian tubes, bladder, colon, and peritoneal lining. The description in the question instead matches Normogonadotropic normoestrogenic anovulation.

rationale: Normogonadotropic normoestrogenic anovulation is the matching concept. Pathologic fracture: A fracture that occurs due to disease process. The description in the question instead matches Six P’s.

Inorganic materials essential for hormone and enzyme production, as well as for bone, muscle, neurological, and cardiac function.

Partially complete proteins: Have enough amino acids to sustain life, but not enough for tissue growth and maintenance. The description in the question instead matches Minerals.

A normal reflex in infants where the big toe bends backward and the other toes fan out when the sole of the foot is stroked.

In Head and Neck Assessment, which concept matches this description?

The bony socket that houses the eyeball and muscles that move the eyeball.

options.rationale: Sagittal plane: A vertical plane running from front to back that divides the body or any of its parts into right and left sides. Laryngopharynx: The portion of the pharynx inferior to the oropharynx and posterior to the larynx that is a passageway for ingested material and air until its inferior end where the digestive and respiratory systems diverge into the esophagus and the larynx. The description in the question instead matches Orbit.
Audiologists: Health care professionals specializing in diagnosing, managing, and treating hearing or balance problems. The description in the question instead matches Orbit.

stem:
In Legal And Ethical Considerations In Mental Health Care, which concept matches this description?

The rights, responsibilities, and legal relationships between private citizens and involves compensation to the injured party.

options.rationale: Unintentional tort: A wrong that occurs when the defendant’s actions or inactions were unreasonably unsafe. Unintentional torts can result from acts of commission (i.e., doing something a reasonable nurse would not have done) or omission (i.e., failing to do something a reasonable nurse would do). The description in the question instead matches Civil law.
Civil law is the matching concept. In this reference context: The rights, responsibilities, and legal relationships between private citizens and involves compensation to the injured party.

Voluntary admission: An individual over age 16 who presents to a psychiatric facility and requests hospitalization. They are considered competent with the capacity to make health care decisions (unless determined otherwise). The description in the question instead matches Civil law.
Justice: A moral obligation to act on the basis of equality and equity and a standard linked to fairness for all in society. The description in the question instead matches Civil law.

rationale: Civil law is the matching concept. In this reference context: The rights, responsibilities, and legal relationships between private citizens and involves compensation to the injured party.

Severe cervical cell abnormalities more likely to progress to cancer.

Epididymitis: Inflammation of the epididymis, the tube that stores and carries sperm. It is often caused by bacterial infections, including STIs like chlamydia and gonorrhea. The description in the question instead matches High-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions.

Cryotherapy: A treatment that uses extreme cold to freeze and destroy abnormal tissue. In reproductive health it can be used to treat precancerous conditions of the cervix. The description in the question instead matches High-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions.

A need for markedly increased amounts of the substance to achieve intoxication or the desired effect and a diminished effect with continued use of the same amount of the substance.

Opioid use disorder: Refers to the chronic use of opioids that causes clinically significant distress or impairment. The description in the question instead matches Tolerance.

Sexual violence: Forcing or attempting to force a partner to take part in a sex act, sexual touching, or a nonphysical sexual event (e.g., sexting) when the partner does not or cannot consent. The description in the question instead matches Tolerance.

Unreasonable confinement or restraint: Refers to the intentional and unnecessary confinement of an individual in a locked room, involuntary separation from their living area, use of physical restraints, or the provision of unnecessary or excessive medication. In Depressive Disorders, which concept matches this description?

A type of psychotherapy that brings people with similar disorders together in a supportive environment to learn how others cope in similar situations.

options.rationale: Seasonal affective disorder: A type of depression causing symptoms during the fall and winter months when there is less sunlight and usually improves with the arrival of spring. SAD is more than just “winter blues.” The symptoms can be distressing and overwhelming and can interfere with daily functioning. The description in the question instead matches Group therapy.

Group therapy is the matching concept. In this reference context: A type of psychotherapy that brings people with similar disorders together in a supportive environment to learn how others cope in similar situations.

Substance/Medication-induced depressive disorder: A type of depression that occurs as a direct result of using, misusing, or withdrawing from certain substances or medications. The description in the question instead matches Group therapy.

Depressive episode: An episode where the person experiences a depressed mood (feeling sad, irritable, empty) or a loss of pleasure or interest in activities for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks. Several other symptoms are also present, which may include poor concentration, feelings of excessive guilt or low self-worth, hopelessness about the future, thoughts about dying or suicide, disrupted sleep, changes in appetite or weight, and feeling especially tired or low in energy. The description in the question instead matches Group therapy.

Root cause analysis: A structured method used to analyze serious adverse events to identify underlying problems that increase the likelihood of errors, while avoiding the trap of focusing on mistakes by individuals. The description in the question instead matches Never events.

Simple human error: According to the Just Culture model, this is an error that occurs when an individual inadvertently does something other than what should have been done. options.rationale: Ventilation-Perfusion Scan: Involves inhalation of a radioactive gas to examine the airways, followed by injection of an isotope intravenously, which is then scanned and tracked to determine blood flow and flow patterns through the lung vessels. Holter Monitor: A portable ECG device that the client wears that records electrical activity of the heart over a period of time, usually 24-48 hours, on an outpatient basis. The client or parent presses a button to record events such as shortness of breath or palpitations. The recording shows arrhythmias and any other normal or abnormal electrical activity that occurs during these recorded events. The description in the question instead matches Electrocardiogram.

stem:
In Sleep And Rest, which concept matches this description?

A record of the time a person goes to sleep, wakes up, and takes naps each day for 1-2 weeks. Timing of activities such as exercising and drinking caffeine or alcohol are also recorded, as well as feelings of sleepiness throughout the day.

options.rationale: Sleep diary is the matching concept. In this reference context: A record of the time a person goes to sleep, wakes up, and takes naps each day for 1-2 weeks. Timing of activities such as exercising and drinking caffeine or alcohol are also recorded, as well as feelings of sleepiness throughout the day.

Sleep-wake homeostasis: The homeostatic sleep drive keeps track of the need for sleep, reminds the body to sleep after a certain time, and regulates sleep intensity. This sleep drive gets stronger every hour a person is awake and causes individuals to sleep longer and more deeply after a period of sleep deprivation. The description in the question instead matches Sleep diary.
Non-REM sleep: Slow-wave sleep when restoration takes place and the body’s temperature, heart rate, and oxygen consumption decrease. The description in the question instead matches Sleep diary.

Circadian rhythms: Body rhythms that direct a wide variety of functions, including wakefulness, body temperature, metabolism, and the release of hormones. They control the timing of sleep, causing individuals to feel sleepy at night and creating a tendency to wake in the morning without an alarm. The description in the question instead matches Sleep diary.

rationale: Sleep diary is the matching concept. In this reference context: A record of the time a person goes to sleep, wakes up, and takes naps each day for 1-2 weeks. Timing of activities such as exercising and drinking caffeine or alcohol are also recorded, as well as feelings of sleepiness throughout the day.

stem:
In Infection, which concept matches this description?

A pathogen that only causes disease in situations that compromise the host’s defenses, such as the body’s protective barriers, immune system, or normal microbiota. Individuals susceptible to opportunistic infections include the very young, the elderly, women who are pregnant, clients undergoing chemotherapy, people with immunodeficiencies (such as acquired immunodeficiency syndrome [AIDS]), clients who are recovering from surgery, and those who have had a breach of protective barriers (such as a severe wound or burn).

options.rationale: Opportunistic pathogen is the matching concept. In this reference context: A pathogen that only causes disease in situations that compromise the host’s defenses, such as the body’s protective barriers, immune system, or normal microbiota. Individuals susceptible to opportunistic infections include the very young, the elderly, women who are pregnant, clients undergoing chemotherapy, people with immunodeficiencies (such as acquired immunodeficiency syndrome [AIDS]), clients who are recovering from surgery, and those who have had a breach of protective barriers (such as a severe wound or burn).

Local infection: Infection confined to a small area of the body, typically near the portal of entry, and usually presents with signs of redness, warmth, swelling, warmth, and pain. Purulent drainage may be present and extensive tissue involvement can cause decreased function. The description in the question instead matches Opportunistic pathogen.

Prodromal period: The disease stage after the incubation period when the pathogen continues to multiply and the host begins to experience general signs and symptoms of illness that result from activation of the immune system, such as fever, pain, soreness, swelling, or inflammation. Usually, such signs and symptoms are too general to indicate a particular disease. The description in the question instead matches Opportunistic pathogen.

Specific adaptive immunity: The immune response that is activated when the nonspecific innate immune response is insufficient to control an infection. There are two types of adaptive responses: the cell-mediated immune response, which is carried out by T cells, and the humoral immune response, which is controlled by activated B cells and antibodies. The description in the question instead matches Opportunistic pathogen.

stem:
Which entry in the reference comparison “Summary of Safe Medication Administration Guidelines” matches this information?

Additional Information: Always verify information whenever you are uncertain or unclear about an order. Consult with the pharmacist, charge nurse, or health care provider, and be sure to resolve all questions before proceeding with medication administration.

options.text: Be cautious and focused when preparing medications
options.rationale: Be cautious and focused when preparing medications: Avoid distractions. Some agencies have a no-interruption zone (NIZ) where health care providers can prepare medications without interruptions. The description in the question instead matches Always clarify an order or procedure that is unclear.

options.text: Use available technology to administer medications
options.rationale: Use available technology to administer medications: Use available technology, such as bar code scanning, when administering medications. Bar code scanning is linked to the patient’s eMAR and provides an extra level of patient safety to prevent wrong medications, incorrect doses, or wrong timing of administration. If error messages occur, it is important to follow up appropriately according to agency policy and not override them. Additionally, it is important to remember that this technology provides an additional layer of safety and should not be substituted for the checking the five rights of medication administration. The description in the question instead matches Always clarify an order or procedure that is unclear.

options.text: Always clarify an order or procedure that is unclear
options.rationale: The matching entry is Always clarify an order or procedure that is unclear. Additional Information: Always verify information whenever you are uncertain or unclear about an order. Consult with the pharmacist, charge nurse, or health care provider, and be sure to resolve all questions before proceeding with medication administration.

Address patient concerns: If a patient questions or expresses concern regarding a medication, stop the procedure and do not administer it. Explore the patient’s concerns, review the provider’s order, and, if necessary, notify the provider. The description in the question instead matches Always clarify an order or procedure that is unclear.

rationale: The matching entry is Always clarify an order or procedure that is unclear. Additional Information: Always verify information whenever you are uncertain or unclear about an order. Description and Indication: Electrodes are placed on the scalp to record electrical activity of the cerebral hemispheres. Each graphic recording represents electrical impulses within the brain. The frequency, amplitude, and characteristics of the brain waves are recorded to evaluate seizure disorders, cerebral disease, brain injury, and brain death.

options.rationale: Electromyography: Records the muscle and nerve integration and electrical activity. Needle electrodes are inserted into the specific muscle units being tested. The description in the question instead matches Electroencephalography.

A surgical procedure to remove part or all of the stapes bone and replace it with a prosthesis to improve hearing.

options.rationale: Audiometry: The testing of a person’s hearing ability, usually by producing sounds of different frequencies and intensities. The description in the question instead matches Stapedectomy.
Otoscopy: The examination of the ear canal and eardrum with an otoscope. The description in the question instead matches Stapedectomy.
Stapedectomy is the matching concept. In this reference context: A surgical procedure to remove part or all of the stapes bone and replace it with a prosthesis to improve hearing.

rationale: Stapedectomy is the matching concept. In this reference context: A surgical procedure to remove part or all of the stapes bone and replace it with a prosthesis to improve hearing.

In Urinary System Terminology, which concept matches this description?

A type of urinary catheter that remains inside the bladder for continuous urine drainage.

options.rationale: Incontinence: The inability to control urination or defecation, leading to involuntary loss of urine or feces. The description in the question instead matches Indwelling catheter.
Urea: A nitrogenous compound produced in the liver as a waste product from the breakdown of proteins, excreted in the urine. The description in the question instead matches Indwelling catheter.
Indwelling catheter is the matching concept. In this reference context: A type of urinary catheter that remains inside the bladder for continuous urine drainage.
Nocturia: The need to wake up and urinate frequently during the night. The description in the question instead matches Indwelling catheter.

Latch that results in painful, cracked nipples; nipples shaped irregularly after nursing; pain during breastfeeding; and a feeling of lack of emptying of the breast.

The study of the digestive system and its disorders.

stem:
In Foundational Mental Health Concepts, which concept matches this description?

A limited ability to engage in activities of daily living (i.e., they cannot maintain personal hygiene, prepare meals, or pay bills) or participate in social events, work, or school.

options.rationale: Major life activities: Activities of daily living such as caring for oneself, performing manual tasks, seeing, hearing, eating, sleeping, walking, standing, lifting, bending, speaking, breathing, learning, reading, concentrating, thinking, communicating, and working. The final section of the large intestine, terminating at the anus.

In Postpartum Care, which concept matches this description?

The muscles in the midline of the abdomen stretch to the point of separation.

options.rationale: Foremilk: Released at the beginning of the breastfeeding session and is high in water and protein content but low in fat. The description in the question instead matches Diastasis recti abdominis.
Heavy lochia: Saturates a peripad in one hour or includes clots larger than a golf ball with lochia. The description in the question instead matches Diastasis recti abdominis.

Lochia serosa: Lochia changes in postpartum Days 4 to 10 that is pinkish-brown and consists of white blood cells, cervical mucus, and discharge from the healing placental site. The description in the question instead matches Diastasis recti abdominis.

The upper middle lobe of the cerebrum, involved in processing sensory information such as touch, temperature, and pain.

Ventricles: Hollow, fluid-filled cavities within the brain that help to protect the brain and reduce its weight. The description in the question instead matches Parietal lobe.

Social workers: Professionals who provide a wide range of services to help people cope with and overcome challenges in their everyday lives, including mental health and substance abuse counseling. The description in the question instead matches Parietal lobe.

Inflammation of the bronchial tubes, often resulting from infection or environmental factors like smoking.

Upper respiratory infection: A viral infection of one or more structures of the upper respiratory system, including the nose, nasal cavities, sinuses, pharynx, and larynx. The description in the question instead matches Bronchitis.

Pleural rub: An abnormal lung sound that is caused by inflammation of the pleura membranes that results in friction as the surfaces rub against each other. The description in the question instead matches Bronchitis.
Exacerbations: Episodes where symptoms of a disease become worse or more severe. The description in the question instead matches Bronchitis.

The part of the ear that includes the cochlea, vestibule, and semicircular canals, responsible for processing sound and maintaining balance.

Anosmia: Loss or impairment of the sense of smell, which can be temporary or permanent. The description in the question instead matches Inner ear.
Audiologists: Health care professionals specializing in diagnosing, managing, and treating hearing or balance problems. The description in the question instead matches Inner ear.

In High-Risk Newborn Care, which concept matches this description?

A bluish discoloration of the lips, tongue, and trunk due to inadequate oxygenation in the blood, requiring immediate medical attention.

Neural tube: A narrow channel that folds and closes during the third and fourth weeks of pregnancy. The description in the question instead matches Central cyanosis.

Very late-onset neonatal sepsis: Sepsis occurring after 28 days, primarily affecting preterm infants in neonatal intensive care units (NICUs). The description in the question instead matches Central cyanosis.
Early-onset neonatal sepsis: Sepsis occurring within the first 72 hours of life, usually acquired from the mother during birth. The description in the question instead matches Central cyanosis.

stem:
Which entry in the reference comparison “Summary of Safe Medication Administration Guidelines” matches this information?

Additional Information: Avoid distractions. Some agencies have a no-interruption zone (NIZ) where health care providers can prepare medications without interruptions.

options.text: Be cautious and focused when preparing medications
options.rationale: The matching entry is Be cautious and focused when preparing medications. Additional Information: Avoid distractions. Some agencies have a no-interruption zone (NIZ) where health care providers can prepare medications without interruptions.

options.text: Perform appropriate patient assessments before medication administration
options.rationale: Perform appropriate patient assessments before medication administration: Assess the patient prior to administering medications to ensure the patient is receiving the correct medication, for the correct reason, and at the correct time. For example, a nurse reviews lab values and performs a cardiac assessment prior to administering cardiac medication. See more information regarding specific patient assessments during parenteral medication administration in the “Applying the Nursing Process” section. The description in the question instead matches Be cautious and focused when preparing medications.

options.text: Use two patient identifiers and follow agency policy for patient identification
options.rationale: Use two patient identifiers and follow agency policy for patient identification: Use at least two patient identifiers before administration and compare information against the medication administration record (MAR). The description in the question instead matches Be cautious and focused when preparing medications.

options.text: Communicate with the patient before and after administration
options.rationale: Communicate with the patient before and after administration: Provide information to the patient about the medication before administering it. Answer their questions regarding usage, dose, and special considerations. Give the patient an opportunity to ask questions and include family members if appropriate. The description in the question instead matches Be cautious and focused when preparing medications.

rationale: The matching entry is Be cautious and focused when preparing medications. Additional Information: Avoid distractions. Some agencies have a no-interruption zone (NIZ) where health care providers can prepare medications without interruptions.

Double vision (i.e., seeing two images of a single object).

stem:
In Reproductive System Alterations, which concept matches this description?

The inability to conceive after 12 months of unprotected sexual intercourse or after six months of unprotected intercourse for women over 35 years old. It also refers to the inability of a woman to carry a pregnancy to live birth.

options.rationale: Cyclical mastalgia: Breast pain associated with the menstrual cycle that begins around the time of ovulation and resolves with menstruation. The description in the question instead matches Infertility.

Infertility is the matching concept. In this reference context: The inability to conceive after 12 months of unprotected sexual intercourse or after six months of unprotected intercourse for women over 35 years old. It also refers to the inability of a woman to carry a pregnancy to live birth.
Menopause: 12 months of amenorrhea that typically occurs between ages 40 and 59, with the average age being 51 years old. The description in the question instead matches Infertility.

Heavy menstrual bleeding: Bleeding that soaks through one more pads or tampons every hour for several hours in a row, has clots the size of a quarter or larger, lasts more than seven days, and requires changing pads or tampons during the night. The description in the question instead matches Infertility.

rationale: Infertility is the matching concept. subject: NP5
stem:
In Depressive Disorders, which concept matches this description?

A type of depression causing symptoms during the fall and winter months when there is less sunlight and usually improves with the arrival of spring. SAD is more than just “winter blues.” The symptoms can be distressing and overwhelming and can interfere with daily functioning.

options.rationale: Electroconvulsive therapy: A medical treatment reserved for clients with severe major depression who have not responded to medications, psychotherapy, or other treatments. It involves a brief electrical stimulation of the brain while the client is under anesthesia. The description in the question instead matches Seasonal affective disorder.

Depressive episode: An episode where the person experiences a depressed mood (feeling sad, irritable, empty) or a loss of pleasure or interest in activities for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks. Several other symptoms are also present, which may include poor concentration, feelings of excessive guilt or low self-worth, hopelessness about the future, thoughts about dying or suicide, disrupted sleep, changes in appetite or weight, and feeling especially tired or low in energy. The description in the question instead matches Seasonal affective disorder.

options.text: Depressive disorder due to another medical condition
options.rationale: Depressive disorder due to another medical condition: When a person experiences a persistent depressed mood or a significant loss of interest or pleasure in activities, and these symptoms are directly caused by a medical illness or condition. The description in the question instead matches Seasonal affective disorder.

In Grief And Loss, which concept matches this description?

A state of chronic and continuous self-sacrifice and/or prolonged exposure to difficult situations that affect a health care professional’s physical, emotional, and spiritual well-being.

options.rationale: Therapeutic communication: A type of professional communication defined as the purposeful, interpersonal, information-transmitting process that leads to client understanding and participation. The description in the question instead matches Compassion fatigue.

Cardiopulmonary resuscitation: Emergency treatment initiated when a client’s breathing stops or their heart stops beating. It may involve chest compressions and mouth-to-mouth breathing, electric shocks to stop lethal cardiac rhythms, breathing tubes to open the airway, or cardiac medications. The description in the question instead matches Compassion fatigue.

Compassion fatigue is the matching concept. In this reference context: A state of chronic and continuous self-sacrifice and/or prolonged exposure to difficult situations that affect a health care professional’s physical, emotional, and spiritual well-being.

Grief: The emotional response to a loss, defined as the individualized and personalized feelings and responses that an individual makes to real, perceived, or anticipated loss. The description in the question instead matches Compassion fatigue.

rationale: Compassion fatigue is the matching concept. In this reference context: A state of chronic and continuous self-sacrifice and/or prolonged exposure to difficult situations that affect a health care professional’s physical, emotional, and spiritual well-being.

The passage of fluid through the circulatory system or lymphatic system to an organ or a tissue.

Pharynx: Commonly known as the throat; a part of the neck and throat that is situated posteriorly to the mouth and nasal cavity and cranially to the esophagus and larynx. The description in the question instead matches Perfusion.
Nasal septum: Separates the left and right sections of the nasal cavity. The description in the question instead matches Perfusion.
Aspirate: To draw in or out using a sucking motion, typically refers to the process of drawing fluid or tissue samples from the body. The description in the question instead matches Perfusion.

In Muscular System Terminology, which concept matches this description?

Paralysis of all four limbs; tetraplegia is another term for the same condition.

options.rationale: Quadriplegia or tetraplegia is the matching concept. In this reference context: Paralysis of all four limbs; tetraplegia is another term for the same condition.

Myasthenia gravis: A chronic autoimmune neuromuscular disease that causes weakness in the skeletal muscles, which are responsible for breathing and moving parts of the body, including the arms and legs. The description in the question instead matches Quadriplegia or tetraplegia.
Dystrophy: A disorder in which an organ or tissue of the body wastes away. The description in the question instead matches Quadriplegia or tetraplegia.
Ptosis: Drooping of the upper eyelid due to paralysis or disease, or as a congenital condition. The description in the question instead matches Quadriplegia or tetraplegia.

subject: CROSS
stem:

An immune response that involves T cells destroying abnormal cells when nonspecific innate immunity and humoral immunity are not effective.

options.rationale: Antigens: Markers that tell the immune system whether something in the body is harmful or not, found on viruses, bacteria, cancer cells, and even normal cells of the body. The description in the question instead matches Cell-mediated response.

Immunization: A method to trigger an individual’s acquired immune response and prevent future disease, often through the administration of a vaccine. The description in the question instead matches Cell-mediated response.

Cell-mediated response is the matching concept. In this reference context: An immune response that involves T cells destroying abnormal cells when nonspecific innate immunity and humoral immunity are not effective.
Tonsillitis: Inflammation of the tonsils, often due to infection. The description in the question instead matches Cell-mediated response.

Breech presentation in which the fetus presents bottom first with legs crossed.

Precipitous labor: Labor and delivery that is extremely rapid, usually less than three hours from start of the contractions to birth. The description in the question instead matches Complete breech.
Gynecoid pelvis: A circular inlet that is considered most favorable for vaginal delivery. The description in the question instead matches Complete breech.

A thick, fan-shaped muscle situated at the chest of the body, making up the bulk of the male chest.

Tendons: Tough bands of fibrous connective tissue that usually connect muscle to bone and are capable of withstanding tension. The description in the question instead matches Pectoralis major.

Spasticity: A feature of altered skeletal muscle performance with a combination of paralysis, increased tendon reflex activity, and hypertonia. The description in the question instead matches Pectoralis major.
Myosin: A type of protein filament that interacts with actin in muscle contraction and is also involved in cellular transport. The description in the question instead matches Pectoralis major.

subject: NP3
stem:
In Perioperative Care, which concept matches this description?

Surgeries where smaller incisions are made, resulting in reduced trauma, faster recovery, and improved client outcomes.

options.rationale: Spinal blocks: Anesthetic medications injected into the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) in the subarachnoid space, providing anesthesia for lower abdominal surgeries, pelvic procedures, hip, and knee surgeries. The description in the question instead matches Minimally invasive surgeries.

Minimally invasive surgeries is the matching concept. In this reference context: Surgeries where smaller incisions are made, resulting in reduced trauma, faster recovery, and improved client outcomes.

Lithotomy position: A position used during procedures to enhance access of the pelvic organs. The client is placed on their back with their buttocks at the edge of the table and their legs abducted 30 to 45 degrees from the midline. The patient’s knees and hips are flexed to about 90 degrees and supported with stirrups or padded leg holders. The description in the question instead matches Minimally invasive surgeries.
Length of stay: A clinical metric that measures the time elapsed between a client’s admission and discharge. The description in the question instead matches Minimally invasive surgeries.

A condition characterized by vaginal bleeding during early pregnancy with the risk of miscarriage.

Inversion of the uterus: A rare but serious condition where the uterus turns inside out, often following childbirth, leading to severe bleeding. The description in the question instead matches Threatened abortion.

subject: NP4
stem:
Which entry in the reference comparison “Common Diagnostic Tests for Nervous System Disorders” matches this information?

Description and Indication: Computer assisted X-ray that provides cross-sectional views of body parts. Used to detect problems such as hemorrhage, tumor, cyst, infarction, edema, brain atrophy, and other abnormalities. Contrast can be used to enhance visualization of brain structures, although scanning is typically first performed without contrast.

options.rationale: Electromyography: Records the muscle and nerve integration and electrical activity. Needle electrodes are inserted into the specific muscle units being tested. Normal, relaxed muscles show no electrical activity, and contracted muscles show electrical activity. The test is indicated for testing for muscle and nerve diseases. The description in the question instead matches CT scan.

Lumbar puncture: Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) is aspirated from the subarachnoid space by a health care provider by inserting a needle between L3-4 or L4-5. Used to examine CSF for infection or presence of blood and measure and reduce CSF pressure. Fluid should be clear and colorless. Pink or blood-tinged CSF may be a sign of subarachnoid hemorrhage, and cloudiness may be due to increased WBCs. The description in the question instead matches CT scan.

The matching entry is CT scan. Description and Indication: Computer assisted X-ray that provides cross-sectional views of body parts. Used to detect problems such as hemorrhage, tumor, cyst, infarction, edema, brain atrophy, and other abnormalities. Contrast can be used to enhance visualization of brain structures, although scanning is typically first performed without contrast.
X-rays: Simple X-ray images of the skull and spine are done to detect fractures, calcifications, bone erosion, and abnormal vascularity. The description in the question instead matches CT scan.

rationale: The matching entry is CT scan. Description and Indication: Computer assisted X-ray that provides cross-sectional views of body parts. Used to detect problems such as hemorrhage, tumor, cyst, infarction, edema, brain atrophy, and other abnormalities. Contrast can be used to enhance visualization of brain structures, although scanning is typically first performed without contrast.

Episodes similar to symptoms of a manic episode, but they are less severe and do not cause significant impairment in social or occupational functioning or require hospitalization.

Interpersonal and social rhythm therapy: Psychotherapy that emphasizes the importance of establishing stable daily routines such as sleeping, waking up, working, and eating meals. The description in the question instead matches Hypomanic episode.

Family-focused therapy: Psychotherapy that focuses on psychoeducation, communication enhancement training, and problem-solving skills. The process of artificially initiating childbirth by stimulating uterine contractions.

Positive signs of pregnancy: Cues provided by the fetus. Signs that directly confirm pregnancy and include auscultation of the fetal heart rate, palpable fetal movement by the examiner, and visualization of the fetus via ultrasound. The description in the question instead matches Induction.

stem:
In Psychotropic Medications, which concept matches this description?

Substances that block the effects of PNS receptors.

options.rationale: Dopamine: A neurotransmitter that plays an essential role in several brain functions, including learning, motor control, reward, emotion, and executive functions. The description in the question instead matches Anticholinergics.
Cholinergics: Substances that stimulate nicotinic and muscarinic receptors and cause effects similar to acetylcholine (ACh). The description in the question instead matches Anticholinergics.
Anticholinergics is the matching concept. In this reference context: Substances that block the effects of PNS receptors.

Neuroleptic malignant syndrome: A rare but fatal adverse effect that can occur at any time during treatment with antipsychotics. It typically develops over a period of days to weeks and resolves in approximately nine days with treatment. Signs include increased temperature, severe muscular rigidity, confusion, agitation, hyperreflexia, elevation in white blood cell count, elevated creatinine phosphokinase, elevated liver enzymes, myoglobinuria, and acute renal failure. The description in the question instead matches Anticholinergics.

Withdrawal symptoms vary in intensity and duration based on the substance(s) used, the duration and amount of use, and the overall health of the individual. The description in the question instead matches Heavy drinking.

Problematic behavior or psychological changes (e.g., impaired motor coordination, euphoria, anxiety, sensation of slowed time, impaired judgment, social withdrawal) that developed during or shortly after cannabis use.

options.rationale: Cannabis intoxication is the matching concept. In this reference context: Problematic behavior or psychological changes (e.g., impaired motor coordination, euphoria, anxiety, sensation of slowed time, impaired judgment, social withdrawal) that developed during or shortly after cannabis use.

Withdrawal/negative affect: The stage at which an individual experiences a negative emotional state in the absence of the substance. The description in the question instead matches Cannabis intoxication.

Substance abuse disorder: Significant impairment or distress from a pattern of substance use (i.e., alcohol, drugs or misuse of prescription medications). The description in the question instead matches Cannabis intoxication.

Alcohol intoxication: Refers to problematic behavioral or psychological changes (e.g., inappropriate sexual or aggressive behavior, mood lability, or impaired judgment) that develop during or shortly thereafter alcohol ingestion. The description in the question instead matches Cannabis intoxication.

A test that checks for problems in the throat, esophagus, stomach, and small intestine.

In Urinary System Terminology, which concept matches this description?

A nitrogenous compound produced in the liver as a waste product from the breakdown of proteins, excreted in the urine.

options.rationale: Hydronephrosis: Swelling of a kidney due to a build-up of urine, often caused by obstruction in the urinary tract. The description in the question instead matches Urea.

Peritoneal dialysis: A form of dialysis where the lining of the abdomen (peritoneum) acts as a filter to remove waste from the blood when the kidneys are not functioning properly. The description in the question instead matches Urea.

Intermittent catheterization: A method of urinary catheterization where a catheter is temporarily inserted into the bladder to drain urine and then removed. The description in the question instead matches Urea.

Involuntary motor symptoms similar to those associated with Parkinson’s disease. Includes symptoms such as akathisia (distressing motor restlessness) and acute dystonia (painful muscle spasms). Often treated with anticholinergic medications such as benztropine and trihexyphenidyl.

Postural instability: Abnormal fixation of posture (stoop when standing), problems with equilibrium, and righting reflex. The description in the question instead matches Extrapyramidal symptoms.

Factors such as income, employment, socioeconomic status, education, food security, housing, social support, discrimination, childhood adversity, the social and physical conditions where people live, and their ability to access acceptable and affordable health care.

Description: Can be used on wounds with minimal or no exudate to retain moisture. Commonly used to secure other dressing materials such as foam.

options.rationale: Hydrogels: Creates a moist wound environment in wounds with little or no exudate. If in gel form, apply directly to the wound and cover with secondary dressing. The description in the question instead matches Transparent films.

Silicone-based dressings: Nonadherent dressing used on moderately to highly exudative wounds. Nontraumatic to wound bed and promotes a moist wound environment. The description in the question instead matches Transparent films.

Alginate/hydrofibers: Nonadherent and highly absorptive for highly exudative wounds. Used for wound packing in full-thickness wounds such as Stage 3 or 4 pressure injuries. The description in the question instead matches Transparent films.

A common office test used to assess how well the lungs work by measuring how much air is inhaled, how much is exhaled, and how quickly it is exhaled.

options.rationale: Spirometry is the matching concept. In this reference context: A common office test used to assess how well the lungs work by measuring how much air is inhaled, how much is exhaled, and how quickly it is exhaled.

Arterial blood gas: A test that measures the amounts of oxygen and carbon dioxide in the blood from an artery. It is used to check how well the lungs are able to move oxygen into the blood and remove carbon dioxide from the blood. The description in the question instead matches Spirometry.
Sputum culture: A test to detect and identify bacteria or fungi that are infecting the lungs or breathing passages. The description in the question instead matches Spirometry.

Chest X-rays: An imaging test that uses small amounts of radiation to produce pictures of the organs, bones, and tissues in the chest area; also called radiographs. The description in the question instead matches Spirometry.

First-time older parents: Older parents in their 40s, 50s and older may have children for several reasons. In Infection, which concept matches this description?

The minimum infection prevention practices that apply to all client care, regardless of suspected or confirmed infection status of the client, in any setting where health care is delivered.

options.rationale: Specific adaptive immunity: The immune response that is activated when the nonspecific innate immune response is insufficient to control an infection. There are two types of adaptive responses: the cell-mediated immune response, which is carried out by T cells, and the humoral immune response, which is controlled by activated B cells and antibodies. The description in the question instead matches Standard precautions.

Standard precautions is the matching concept. In this reference context: The minimum infection prevention practices that apply to all client care, regardless of suspected or confirmed infection status of the client, in any setting where health care is delivered.

Prodromal period: The disease stage after the incubation period when the pathogen continues to multiply and the host begins to experience general signs and symptoms of illness that result from activation of the immune system, such as fever, pain, soreness, swelling, or inflammation. Usually, such signs and symptoms are too general to indicate a particular disease. The description in the question instead matches Standard precautions.

Opportunistic pathogen: A pathogen that only causes disease in situations that compromise the host’s defenses, such as the body’s protective barriers, immune system, or normal microbiota. Individuals susceptible to opportunistic infections include the very young, the elderly, women who are pregnant, clients undergoing chemotherapy, people with immunodeficiencies (such as acquired immunodeficiency syndrome [AIDS]), clients who are recovering from surgery, and those who have had a breach of protective barriers (such as a severe wound or burn). The description in the question instead matches Standard precautions.

rationale: Standard precautions is the matching concept. In this reference context: The minimum infection prevention practices that apply to all client care, regardless of suspected or confirmed infection status of the client, in any setting where health care is delivered.

Actions to decrease the spread of infection to others. This includes covering the mouth and nose with a tissue when coughing and sneezing and disposing of the tissue in the trash. If a tissue is not available, clients should sneeze into their inner elbow instead of hands.

options.rationale: Respiratory etiquette is the matching concept. In this reference context: Actions to decrease the spread of infection to others. This includes covering the mouth and nose with a tissue when coughing and sneezing and disposing of the tissue in the trash. If a tissue is not available, clients should sneeze into their inner elbow instead of hands.

Post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis: Inflammation of the glomerulus of the kidneys as a result of an untreated strep infection; leads to edema, increased blood pressure, and alterations in kidney function. The description in the question instead matches Respiratory etiquette.
Oophoritis: Inflammation of the ovaries, associated with mumps. The description in the question instead matches Respiratory etiquette.
Infectious mononucleosis: A viral infection commonly caused by Epstein-Barr virus. The description in the question instead matches Respiratory etiquette.

rationale: Respiratory etiquette is the matching concept. In this reference context: Actions to decrease the spread of infection to others. This includes covering the mouth and nose with a tissue when coughing and sneezing and disposing of the tissue in the trash. If a tissue is not available, clients should sneeze into their inner elbow instead of hands.
keyPoint: Respiratory etiquette: Actions to decrease the spread of infection to others. subject: NP5
stem:
In Mental Health Concepts, which concept matches this description?

Refers to purposely injuring one’s body, such as cutting oneself with a sharp object.

options.rationale: Spirituality: A dynamic and intrinsic aspect of humanity through which persons seek ultimate meaning, purpose, and transcendence and experience relationships to self, family, others, community, society, nature, and the significant or sacred. The description in the question instead matches Self-harm.
Self-harm is the matching concept. In this reference context: Refers to purposely injuring one’s body, such as cutting oneself with a sharp object.

Adverse childhood experiences: Stressful and potentially traumatic events experienced during childhood such as abuse, neglect, or growing up in a household with violence, mental illness, substance misuse, incarceration, or divorce. ACEs can affect an individual’s mental health and are linked to chronic health problems, mental illness, and substance misuse in adulthood. The description in the question instead matches Self-harm.

Competency: A legal term related to the degree of cognitive ability an individual has to make decisions, carry out specific acts, or provide informed consent. The description in the question instead matches Self-harm.

rationale: Self-harm is the matching concept. In this reference context: Refers to purposely injuring one’s body, such as cutting oneself with a sharp object.

Activities aimed to facilitate movement of specific joints and promote mobility of extremities.

Active assist range-of-motion exercise: A client’s joint receiving partial assistance in movement from an outside force. The description in the question instead matches Range-of-motion exercises.
Plantar flexion: The movement of the foot in which the foot or toes flex downward toward the sole. The description in the question instead matches Range-of-motion exercises.

Transferring: The action of a client moving from one surface to another. This includes moving from a bed into a chair or moving from one chair to another. The description in the question instead matches Range-of-motion exercises.

A sphincter muscle that separates the small intestine and the large intestine, controlling the passage of chyme.

Salivary glands: Small glands in the mucous membranes of the mouth and tongue that secrete saliva directly into the oral cavity or indirectly through salivary ducts. The description in the question instead matches Ileocecal valve.

stem:
In Autonomic Nervous System, which concept matches this description?

Stimulation causes increases speed of conduction between SA and AV node.

options.rationale: Involuntary responses: Responses that the brain controls without the need for conscious thought. The description in the question instead matches Dromotropic.
Sensory neurons: Sense the environment and conduct signals to the brain that become a conscious perception of that stimulus. The description in the question instead matches Dromotropic.

Chronotropic: Drugs may change the heart rate and rhythm by affecting the electrical conduction system of the heart and the nerves that influence it, such as by changing the rhythm (increasing) produced by the sinoatrial node. Positive chronotropes increase heart rate; negative chronotropes decrease heart rate. The description in the question instead matches Dromotropic.

rationale: Dromotropic is the matching concept. In this reference context: Stimulation causes increases speed of conduction between SA and AV node.

A progressive neurodegenerative disease that affects nerve cells in the brain and spinal cord, causing muscle weakness and atrophy.

Hematoma: A solid swelling of clotted blood within the tissues, often caused by an injury. The description in the question instead matches Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.

Aphasia: A condition characterized by either partial or total loss of the ability to communicate verbally or using written words. The description in the question instead matches Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.

subject: NP5
stem:
In Thought Disorders, which concept matches this description?

An episode of psychosis that can include delusions, hallucinations, disorganized speech, and grossly disorganized or catatonic behavior.

options.rationale: Psychotic episode is the matching concept. In this reference context: An episode of psychosis that can include delusions, hallucinations, disorganized speech, and grossly disorganized or catatonic behavior.

First-generation antipsychotics: Also referred to as “typical antipsychotics”; this class of medications has several potential adverse effects due to the blockage of dopamine receptors. Medication is prescribed based on the client’s ability to tolerate the adverse effects. The description in the question instead matches Psychotic episode.
Catatonia: A pronounced increase or decrease in the rate and amount of movement; excessive movement is purposeless. The description in the question instead matches Psychotic episode.

Coordinated specialty care: A general term used to describe recovery-oriented treatment programs for people with first-episode psychosis, an early stage of schizophrenia. The description in the question instead matches Psychotic episode.

rationale: Psychotic episode is the matching concept. In this reference context: An episode of psychosis that can include delusions, hallucinations, disorganized speech, and grossly disorganized or catatonic behavior.

Mild cervical cell abnormalities often caused by HPV.

Bartholin’s glands: Glands located near the vaginal opening that secrete fluid to lubricate the vagina. The description in the question instead matches Low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions.

Adnexa: The structures adjacent to an organ. In gynecology, it refers to the ovaries, Fallopian tubes, and ligaments attached to the uterus. The description in the question instead matches Low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions.

The process of how an infection spreads based on six links of transmission: Infectious Agent, Reservoir, Portal of Exit, Modes of Transmission, Portal of Entry, and Susceptible Host.

Mechanical lifts that support a client weighing 600 or more pounds.

Removing an undesirable stimulus from the environment to encourage a specific behavior.

Moro reflex: In response to a loud noise, the infant’s arms and legs extend and their back arches; also called the startle reflex. The description in the question instead matches Negative reinforcement.
