subject: CROSS
stem:
In Initiate IV Therapy, which concept matches this description?

A condition that occurs when a nonvesicant solution (IV solution) is inadvertently administered into surrounding tissue. Signs and symptoms include pain, swelling, redness, the skin surrounding the insertion site is cool to touch, there is a change in the quality or flow of IV, the skin is tight around the IV site, IV fluid is leaking from IV site, or there are frequent alarms on the IV pump.

options.rationale: Catheter-related bloodstream infection: An infection caused by microorganisms introduced into the bloodstream through the puncture site, the hub, or contaminated IV tubing or IV solution, leading to bacteremia or sepsis. A CR-BSI is a hospital-acquired preventable infection and considered an adverse event. The description in the question instead matches Infiltration.

Infiltration is the matching concept. In this reference context: A condition that occurs when a nonvesicant solution (IV solution) is inadvertently administered into surrounding tissue. Signs and symptoms include pain, swelling, redness, the skin surrounding the insertion site is cool to touch, there is a change in the quality or flow of IV, the skin is tight around the IV site, IV fluid is leaking from IV site, or there are frequent alarms on the IV pump.

Vesicant medications: Certain medications such as antineoplastic drugs, antibiotics, electrolytes, and vasopressors that can cause severe tissue injury or destruction. The description in the question instead matches Infiltration.

Phlebitis: The inflammation of the vein’s inner lining, the tunica intima. Clinical indications are localized redness, pain, heat, and swelling that can track up the vein leading to a palpable venous cord. The description in the question instead matches Infiltration.

rationale: Infiltration is the matching concept. In this reference context: A condition that occurs when a nonvesicant solution (IV solution) is inadvertently administered into surrounding tissue. Signs and symptoms include pain, swelling, redness, the skin surrounding the insertion site is cool to touch, there is a change in the quality or flow of IV, the skin is tight around the IV site, IV fluid is leaking from IV site, or there are frequent alarms on the IV pump.

subject: NP5
stem:
In Anxiety Disorders, which concept matches this description?

A condition when people fail to speak in specific social situations despite having normal language skills.

options.rationale: Separation anxiety disorder: A condition where an individual has a fear about being separated from people to whom they are attached. The description in the question instead matches Selective mutism.
Selective mutism is the matching concept. In this reference context: A condition when people fail to speak in specific social situations despite having normal language skills.

Social anxiety disorder: A type of anxiety disorder characterized by extreme anxiety or fear related to social situations where they may be scrutinized by others. The description in the question instead matches Selective mutism.

Obsessive-compulsive disorder: A common chronic disorder in which a person has uncontrollable, reoccurring thoughts (obsessions) and/or behaviors (compulsions) they feel the urge to repeat over and over. Performing the compulsive behaviors often brings the person brief relief from the anxiety the obsessive thoughts cause them. The description in the question instead matches Selective mutism.

rationale: Selective mutism is the matching concept. In this reference context: A condition when people fail to speak in specific social situations despite having normal language skills.

Interventions that target individuals who have a high probability of developing disease.

Tertiary prevention: Interventions implemented for symptomatic clients to reduce the severity of the disease and potential long-term complications. The description in the question instead matches Indicated prevention.

Healthy community: A community in which local groups from all parts of the community work together to prevent disease and make healthy living options accessible. The description in the question instead matches Indicated prevention.

Focus groups: A systematic way of collecting data through small group discussion. Focus group participants are chosen to represent a larger group of people. The description in the question instead matches Indicated prevention.

Nursing problems currently occurring with the client.

Description: The caregiver places one or two hands on the client’s body to help with balance but provides no other assistance to perform the functional mobility task.

In Muscular System Terminology, which concept matches this description?

A major muscle of the upper arm that extends the elbow.

Spasticity: A feature of altered skeletal muscle performance with a combination of paralysis, increased tendon reflex activity, and hypertonia. The description in the question instead matches Triceps brachii.
Tendons: Tough bands of fibrous connective tissue that usually connect muscle to bone and are capable of withstanding tension. The description in the question instead matches Triceps brachii.

subject: NP2
stem:
In Reproductive Concepts, which concept matches this description?

A test used to detect the presence of human papillomavirus (HPV) in cervical cells.

options.rationale: HPV test is the matching concept. In this reference context: A test used to detect the presence of human papillomavirus (HPV) in cervical cells.

Hydrocele: A fluid-filled sac around a testicle that causes swelling in the scrotum. It is usually painless and may resolve on its own or require surgical treatment. The description in the question instead matches HPV test.

Transurethral incision of the prostate: A surgical procedure used to treat benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH). Small cuts are made in the prostate to widen the urethra and improve urine flow. The description in the question instead matches HPV test.

Cold knife conization: A surgical procedure in which a cone-shaped piece of abnormal tissue is removed from the cervix using a scalpel. This is often done to diagnose or treat precancerous conditions of the cervix. The description in the question instead matches HPV test.

rationale: HPV test is the matching concept. In this reference context: A test used to detect the presence of human papillomavirus (HPV) in cervical cells.

subject: NP5
stem:
In Urinary System Terminology, which concept matches this description?

A substance or medication that increases the production and excretion of urine, used to treat conditions like high blood pressure.

options.rationale: Diuretic is the matching concept. In this reference context: A substance or medication that increases the production and excretion of urine, used to treat conditions like high blood pressure.

Urodynamic flow testing: A series of diagnostic tests that assess the function of the bladder and urethra, specifically focusing on urine storage and release. The description in the question instead matches Diuretic.
Urinary catheterization: The process of inserting a catheter into the bladder through the urethra for the purpose of draining urine. The description in the question instead matches Diuretic.

Urine dip: A quick, initial screening test using a dipstick to detect abnormalities in urine, such as the presence of blood, protein, or signs of infection. The description in the question instead matches Diuretic.

A type of fracture when the broken bone punctures the skin.

Withdrawal symptoms that occur when chronic pain medication is suddenly reduced or stopped because of physiological adaptations that occur from chronic exposure to the medication.

A rare but life-threatening condition caused by bacterial toxins.

A vertical plane running from front to back that divides the body or any of its parts into right and left sides. If this vertical plane runs directly down the middle of the body, it is called the midsagittal or median plane. If the plane divides the body into unequal right and left sides, it is called a parasagittal plane or longitudinal section.

Theory by Ramona Mercer, which suggests that early skin-to-skin contact, breastfeeding, and minimizing time apart promote bonding, decrease maternal anxiety, and encourage attainment of the maternal role.

Latch: The way a newborn attaches to the mother’s breast for feeding, which is important for efficient milk transfer and preventing nipple soreness. The description in the question instead matches Maternal Role Attainment Theory.

In Urinary System Terminology, which concept matches this description?

Infections that occur more often or are more severe in people with weakened immune systems.

options.rationale: Interstitial space: The space between individual cells in the tissues. The description in the question instead matches Opportunistic infection.

Antibodies: Proteins that are very specific to the antigens they recognize and destroy, fitting onto the antigen like a key to a lock. The description in the question instead matches Opportunistic infection.
Metastasize: The spread of malignant cells through the blood or lymphatic system and invasion in other areas of the body. The description in the question instead matches Opportunistic infection.

A cancer caused by the herpes virus, typically observed in individuals with weakened immune systems.

options.rationale: Hodgkin lymphoma: Cancer originating from the lymphatic system, characterized by out-of-control growth of lymphocytes, causing swollen lymph nodes and growths throughout the body. The description in the question instead matches Kaposi’s sarcoma.

Cell-mediated response: An immune response that involves T cells destroying abnormal cells when nonspecific innate immunity and humoral immunity are not effective. The description in the question instead matches Kaposi’s sarcoma.

Hypersensitivity: An exaggerated immune response triggered by exposure to a specific antigen, which can damage normal tissues and cause a range of health issues. The description in the question instead matches Kaposi’s sarcoma.
Kaposi’s sarcoma is the matching concept. In this reference context: A cancer caused by the herpes virus, typically observed in individuals with weakened immune systems.

subject: NP4
stem:
Which entry in the reference comparison “Common Diagnostic Tests for Nervous System Disorders” matches this information?

Description and Indication: Simple X-ray images of the skull and spine are done to detect fractures, calcifications, bone erosion, and abnormal vascularity.

options.rationale: Positron emission tomography: Measures metabolic activity of the brain to determine cell death or damage. A radioactive isotope is injected that shows up as a bright spot on the image if abnormal activity is occurring. Indicated for clients with stroke, Alzheimer’s disease, seizure disorders, Parkinson’s disease, infection, and tumors. The description in the question instead matches X-rays.

Electroneurography: Measures the conduction velocity of peripheral nerves. A brief electrical stimulus is initiated at the distal portion of the sensory nerve being tested. A recording of the depolarization wave is taken at a point proximal to the stimulus. The time between the initial stimulus and the beginning of the depolarization wave is measured (i.e., nerve conduction velocity). Damaged nerves will have slower conduction velocities. The description in the question instead matches X-rays.
The matching entry is X-rays. Description and Indication: Simple X-ray images of the skull and spine are done to detect fractures, calcifications, bone erosion, and abnormal vascularity.

Carotid artery duplex scan: Combines ultrasound and Doppler technology to evaluate the degree of stenosis (narrowing) of the carotid and vertebral arteries. Using transducer gel, a probe is placed over the common carotid artery and moved slowly along its length. Frequency of reflected ultrasound signal corresponds with the velocity of blood flow. Increased blood flow velocity may indicate stenosis or partial or total occlusion of the vessels. The description in the question instead matches X-rays.

rationale: The matching entry is X-rays. Description and Indication: Simple X-ray images of the skull and spine are done to detect fractures, calcifications, bone erosion, and abnormal vascularity.

Vitiligo: A disease that causes loss of skin color in blotches. The description in the question instead matches Bacteria.
Virus: A microorganism that spreads infection by invading the body’s cells and replicating. The description in the question instead matches Bacteria.

A surgical procedure performed to deliver a fetus through incisions made in the mother’s abdomen and uterus when a vaginal birth poses risks to the mother or fetus or when complications occur during labor.

options.rationale: Focal points: The client centers their attention on a picture or an object in the room and concentrates on breathing through the contraction. The description in the question instead matches Cesarean section.

subject: NP5

Strategies used to manage one’s emotional response to stressors, such as participating in mindfulness, meditation, or yoga; using humor and jokes; seeking spiritual or religious pursuits; engaging in physical activity or breathing exercises; and seeking social support.

options.rationale: Behavioral restraints: Restraints used to manage violent or self-destructive behavior that poses an immediate danger to a client or others. The description in the question instead matches Emotion-focused coping.

Environmental stressors: Aspects of a client’s surroundings that may increase mental or emotional strain, induce the stress response, and possibly impact their health care. The description in the question instead matches Emotion-focused coping.
Lack of insight: The inability to perceive changes in one’s own feelings, behavior, or personality. The description in the question instead matches Emotion-focused coping.

Emotion-focused coping is the matching concept. subject: NP5
stem:
In Substance Use Disorders, which concept matches this description?

Severe substance use disorders; a chronic brain disease that has the potential for both recurrence (relapse) and recovery.

options.rationale: Dependence: A condition that develops with chronic uses of a substance that causes a person to experience withdrawal symptoms if the substance is suddenly stopped. The description in the question instead matches Addiction.
Addiction is the matching concept. In this reference context: Severe substance use disorders; a chronic brain disease that has the potential for both recurrence (relapse) and recovery.

Remission: The status of individuals with severe substance use disorders who overcome their disorder with effective treatment and regain health and social function. The description in the question instead matches Addiction.

Alcohol intoxication: Refers to problematic behavioral or psychological changes (e.g., inappropriate sexual or aggressive behavior, mood lability, or impaired judgment) that develop during or shortly thereafter alcohol ingestion. The description in the question instead matches Addiction.

rationale: Addiction is the matching concept. In this reference context: Severe substance use disorders; a chronic brain disease that has the potential for both recurrence (relapse) and recovery.

In Childhood Respiratory Disorders, which concept matches this description?

Reduces surface tension of alveoli and prevents alveolar collapse.

Chemokine: A specific type of cytokine; acts as a chemical messenger. The description in the question instead matches Surfactant.
Aspiration pneumonia: Pneumonia that occurs when food or liquid is breathed into the airways or lungs, instead of being swallowed. The description in the question instead matches Surfactant.

Fremitus: Changes in vibration when certain words are spoken while the chest is being palpated; its presence can indicate underlying lung issues. The description in the question instead matches Surfactant.

subject: NP5
stem:
In Mental Health Conditions, which concept matches this description?

A neurodevelopmental disorder that can significantly affect a person’s behavior and their ability to communicate and socialize. Occurs in all ethnic, racial, and economic groups.

options.rationale: Autism spectrum disorder is the matching concept. In this reference context: A neurodevelopmental disorder that can significantly affect a person’s behavior and their ability to communicate and socialize. Occurs in all ethnic, racial, and economic groups.

Oppositional defiant disorder: A mental health condition referring to a pattern of angry/irritable mood, argumentative/defiant behaviors, or vindictiveness lasting at least six months. The description in the question instead matches Autism spectrum disorder.

Compulsions: Repetitive behaviors that a person with obsessive-compulsive disorder feels the urge to do in response to an obsessive thought. The description in the question instead matches Autism spectrum disorder.

Social anxiety disorder: A type of anxiety disorder characterized by extreme anxiety or fear related to social situations where they may be scrutinized by others. The description in the question instead matches Autism spectrum disorder.

rationale: Autism spectrum disorder is the matching concept. In this reference context: A neurodevelopmental disorder that can significantly affect a person’s behavior and their ability to communicate and socialize. Occurs in all ethnic, racial, and economic groups.

subject: NP2
stem:
In High-Risk Perinatal Client Care, which concept matches this description?

The medical or surgical termination of a pregnancy.

options.rationale: Salpingectomy: A surgical procedure to remove one or both Fallopian tubes; often performed to treat ectopic pregnancy or prevent future complications. The description in the question instead matches Induced abortion.

Cervical dilation and curettage: A surgical procedure to remove tissue from the uterus; often performed after miscarriage or abortion. The description in the question instead matches Induced abortion.

Fundal massage: A procedure of applying firm pressure to the fundus to induce a uterine contraction and to stop the blood from pumping out of the spiral arteries. The goal is to cause the uterus to contract into the size of a small, hard ball. The description in the question instead matches Induced abortion.
Induced abortion is the matching concept. In this reference context: The medical or surgical termination of a pregnancy.

stem:
In Reproductive Concepts, which concept matches this description?

The process where a sperm cell penetrates and merges with an egg cell, resulting in the formation of a zygote.

Myometrium: The muscular layer of the uterus responsible for contractions during menstruation and childbirth. The description in the question instead matches Fertilization.
Vas deferens: The duct that carries sperm from the epididymis to the urethra in preparation for ejaculation. The description in the question instead matches Fertilization.
Orgasm: The peak of sexual pleasure, often accompanied by the release of tension and involuntary muscle contractions. The description in the question instead matches Fertilization.

In Respiratory System Terminology, which concept matches this description?

A medical instrument used for listening to the internal sounds of an organism, typically used for heart and lung sounds.

options.rationale: Aspiration: The inhalation of food, liquid, or other material into the respiratory tract. The description in the question instead matches Stethoscope.

Bilevel positive airway pressure: A form of noninvasive ventilation that provides two levels of air pressure, one for inhalation and a lower one for exhalation, used in the treatment of sleep apnea and other respiratory problems. The description in the question instead matches Stethoscope.
Stethoscope is the matching concept. In this reference context: A medical instrument used for listening to the internal sounds of an organism, typically used for heart and lung sounds.
Cyanosis: A bluish discoloration of the skin and mucous membranes resulting from poor circulation or inadequate oxygenation of the blood. The description in the question instead matches Stethoscope.

rationale: Stethoscope is the matching concept. In this reference context: A medical instrument used for listening to the internal sounds of an organism, typically used for heart and lung sounds.

A medical condition characterized by a decreased number of platelets in the blood.

Aplastic anemia: A relatively rare but serious medical condition characterized by a significant reduction or absence of all three major blood cell types: red blood cells (RBCs), white blood cells (WBCs), and platelets. The description in the question instead matches Thrombocytopenia.
Koilonychia: Thin, brittle, or spoon-shaped nails often resulting from iron-deficiency anemia. The description in the question instead matches Thrombocytopenia.

A pregnancy in which a fertilized egg implants in the uterus but does not develop into an embryo.

Late postpartum hemorrhage: Excessive bleeding occurring more than 24 hours and up to twelve weeks postpartum. The description in the question instead matches Blighted ovum.

The innermost layer of the eye, containing photoreceptors and nerve cells for initial processing of visual stimuli.

Auricle: The large fleshy structure on the lateral aspect of the head, directing sound waves into the ear canal. The description in the question instead matches Retina.
Vestibulocochlear nerve: The nerve that carries auditory and balance information from the inner ear to the brain. The description in the question instead matches Retina.

subject: CROSS

In Autonomic Nervous System, which concept matches this description?

Stimulation causes increased force of contraction.

options.rationale: Nonselective beta-blockers: Medications that block both Beta-1 and Beta-2 receptors, thus affecting both the heart and lungs. The description in the question instead matches Inotropic.
Involuntary responses: Responses that the brain controls without the need for conscious thought. The description in the question instead matches Inotropic.

Adrenergic agonist: Mimics the effects of the body’s natural SNS stimulation on alpha (α)- and beta (β)-receptors. Also called sympathomimetics. The description in the question instead matches Inotropic.

Formal questionnaires or checklists based on research that ask questions about a child’s development, including language, movement, thinking, behavior, and emotions.

options.rationale: Reflexes: Involuntary movements in response to stimulation. The description in the question instead matches Developmental screening.

Developmental screening is the matching concept. In this reference context: Formal questionnaires or checklists based on research that ask questions about a child’s development, including language, movement, thinking, behavior, and emotions.

Moro reflex: In response to a loud noise, the infant’s arms and legs extend and their back arches; also called the startle reflex. The description in the question instead matches Developmental screening.

Bibliotherapy: A behavioral intervention that uses books to help children express feelings in a supportive environment, gain insight into feelings and behavior, and learn new ways to cope with difficult situations. The description in the question instead matches Developmental screening.

subject: NP4
stem:
In Nervous System Alterations, which concept matches this description?

A rare autoimmune disease that causes muscle weakness and sometimes paralysis.

options.rationale: Epilepsy: A chronic disorder that is defined by at least two unprovoked seizures occurring at least 24 hours apart and in which groups of nerve cells, or neurons, in the brain sometimes send the wrong signals and cause recurrent, unpredictable, and unprovoked seizures. The description in the question instead matches Guillain-Barré syndrome.
Generalized seizures: Involve abnormal electrical activity in both cerebral hemispheres of the brain. The description in the question instead matches Guillain-Barré syndrome.

Glasgow Coma Scale: A standardized tool used to objectively assess and continually monitor a client’s level of consciousness when damage has occurred, such as after a head injury or a cerebrovascular accident (stroke). The description in the question instead matches Guillain-Barré syndrome.
Guillain-Barré syndrome is the matching concept. In this reference context: A rare autoimmune disease that causes muscle weakness and sometimes paralysis.

Counties without a hospital or birth center offering obstetric care and without any obstetric providers.

Constipation that is not caused by an underlying disease process.

options.rationale: Conjunctivitis: Inflammation of the conjunctiva of the eye; commonly known as pink eye. The description in the question instead matches Functional constipation.

Nasolacrimal duct obstruction: A common condition affecting up to 20% of newborn clients. Chronic conditions have a slow onset and may gradually worsen over time.

stem:
In Sleep And Rest, which concept matches this description?

The homeostatic sleep drive keeps track of the need for sleep, reminds the body to sleep after a certain time, and regulates sleep intensity. This sleep drive gets stronger every hour a person is awake and causes individuals to sleep longer and more deeply after a period of sleep deprivation.

options.rationale: Non-REM sleep: Slow-wave sleep when restoration takes place and the body’s temperature, heart rate, and oxygen consumption decrease. The description in the question instead matches Sleep-wake homeostasis.

Sleep diary: A record of the time a person goes to sleep, wakes up, and takes naps each day for 1-2 weeks. Timing of activities such as exercising and drinking caffeine or alcohol are also recorded, as well as feelings of sleepiness throughout the day. The description in the question instead matches Sleep-wake homeostasis.

Sleep-wake homeostasis is the matching concept. In this reference context: The homeostatic sleep drive keeps track of the need for sleep, reminds the body to sleep after a certain time, and regulates sleep intensity. This sleep drive gets stronger every hour a person is awake and causes individuals to sleep longer and more deeply after a period of sleep deprivation.

Circadian rhythms: Body rhythms that direct a wide variety of functions, including wakefulness, body temperature, metabolism, and the release of hormones. They control the timing of sleep, causing individuals to feel sleepy at night and creating a tendency to wake in the morning without an alarm. The description in the question instead matches Sleep-wake homeostasis.

In this reference context: The homeostatic sleep drive keeps track of the need for sleep, reminds the body to sleep after a certain time, and regulates sleep intensity. subject: NP3
stem:
Which entry in the reference comparison “Blood Products, Used for life-threatening hemorrhage where oxygen-carrying capacity, coagulation factors, platelets, and volume expansion are all needed. Whole blood contains approximately 150 mL of plasma, which provides volume expansion and stabilization of clotting factors.” matches this information?

Actions/Indications/Benefits: Provides antibodies the client cannot make on their own (i.e., “humoral immunodeficiency”). Indicated as replacement therapy for immunodeficiencies, autoimmune conditions such as immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) and autoimmune hemolytic anemia (AIHA), Guillain-Barré syndrome, or chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy (CIDP).

options.rationale: Autologous: Provides patient’s own blood to prevent potential transfusion reactions but has risk for bacterial infection. Used to replace blood loss during planned elective surgery. The description in the question instead matches Intravenous Immunoglobulin.

Cryoprecipitate: Provides Factor VIII, fibrinogen, vWF, and Factor XIII. Indicated for Hemophilia A, von Willebrand’s disease, and Factor XIII deficiency. Also used as a part of “Mass Transfusion” protocols where clotting factor deficiencies are common. One pool increases fibrinogen approximately 50 mg/dL. The description in the question instead matches Intravenous Immunoglobulin.

Fresh Frozen Plasma: Increases clotting factors and expands blood volume. Indicated for clients with bleeding disorders, thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP), and life-threatening hemorrhage in patients who have significant coagulation deficiencies. Also used to reverse a client’s elevated INR when it needs to be brought down quickly to prevent complications from occurring. One unit increases clotting factors approximately 2-5%. Plasma is typically frozen within hours of donation to preserve the clotting factors and is thawed by the lab prior to administration. The description in the question instead matches Intravenous Immunoglobulin.

The matching entry is Intravenous Immunoglobulin. Actions/Indications/Benefits: Provides antibodies the client cannot make on their own (i.e., “humoral immunodeficiency”). Indicated as replacement therapy for immunodeficiencies, autoimmune conditions such as immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) and autoimmune hemolytic anemia (AIHA), Guillain-Barré syndrome, or chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy (CIDP).

rationale: The matching entry is Intravenous Immunoglobulin. Actions/Indications/Benefits: Provides antibodies the client cannot make on their own (i.e., “humoral immunodeficiency”). Indicated as replacement therapy for immunodeficiencies, autoimmune conditions such as immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) and autoimmune hemolytic anemia (AIHA), Guillain-Barré syndrome, or chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy (CIDP).
keyPoint: Intravenous Immunoglobulin: Provides antibodies the client cannot make on their own (i.e., “humoral immunodeficiency”). options.rationale: Infiltration: A condition that occurs when a nonvesicant solution (IV solution) is inadvertently administered into surrounding tissue. The description in the question instead matches Phlebitis.

Catheter-related bloodstream infection: An infection caused by microorganisms introduced into the bloodstream through the puncture site, the hub, or contaminated IV tubing or IV solution, leading to bacteremia or sepsis. A CR-BSI is a hospital-acquired preventable infection and considered an adverse event. The description in the question instead matches Phlebitis.

Significance: Characterized by quivering ventricles with no effective contractions and no cardiac output. This is the most dangerous arrhythmia because of lack of cardiac output and requires immediate initiation of CPR and emergency response.

Second-Degree Heart Block: Characterized by dropped ventricular beats that can result in decreased cardiac output. May require a pacemaker if symptomatic. The description in the question instead matches Ventricular Fibrillation.

subject: CROSS
stem:
In Aseptic Technique, which concept matches this description?

Techniques used to eliminate every potential microorganism in and around a sterile field while maintaining objects and areas as free from microorganisms as possible. This technique is the standard of care for surgical procedures, invasive wound management, and central line care.

Aseptic technique: The purposeful reduction of pathogen numbers while preventing microorganism transfer from one person or object to another. This technique is commonly used to perform invasive procedures, such as IV starts or urinary catheterization. The description in the question instead matches Sterile technique.

Taking-hold: Phase that occurs four to ten days after delivery when the postpartum client’s focus turns to the newborn. The client becomes more confident in caring for the newborn and more comfortable in the maternal role but may continue to seek support from family members and friends who can provide guidance and understanding. (, ). The description in the question instead matches Uterine involution.

Letting-go: Begins several weeks after delivery as the client establishes a new parental role identity and focuses on the family unit. In Provide Care for Clients Experiencing Acute and Chronic Health Conditions, which concept matches this description?

The skills and abilities to live independently.

options.rationale: Adaptive behavior is the matching concept. In this reference context: The skills and abilities to live independently.
Perseverating: The act of repeating a task or thought over and over. The description in the question instead matches Adaptive behavior.
Pocketing: The act of keeping food or medications in one’s cheeks and not swallowing it. The description in the question instead matches Adaptive behavior.
Wandering: The simple act of a person walking around with no purpose due to their confusion regarding their location or environment. The description in the question instead matches Adaptive behavior.

rationale: Adaptive behavior is the matching concept. In this reference context: The skills and abilities to live independently.
keyPoint: Adaptive behavior: The skills and abilities to live independently.

When a PVC occurs on the T wave.

R-R interval: The interval that represents the duration between the ventricular heartbeats. The description in the question instead matches R on T phenomenon.
Tricuspid valve: The valve between the right atrium and right ventricle. The description in the question instead matches R on T phenomenon.
R on T phenomenon is the matching concept. In this reference context: When a PVC occurs on the T wave.

subject: NP3
stem:
In Lymphatic & Immune Systems Terminology, which concept matches this description?

An organ in the upper far left part of the abdomen, to the left of the stomach, which filters blood and is involved in immune response.

options.rationale: Apoptosis: Programmed cell death that is disrupted in some cancers, allowing malignant cells to avoid natural cell death and continue uncontrolled growth. The description in the question instead matches Spleen.

Phagocytosis: The process by which a cell uses its plasma membrane to engulf a large particle, forming an internal compartment known as a phagosome. The description in the question instead matches Spleen.
Spleen is the matching concept. In this reference context: An organ in the upper far left part of the abdomen, to the left of the stomach, which filters blood and is involved in immune response.

Lymphatic system: A network of organs, lymph nodes, lymph ducts, and lymph vessels that produce and transport lymph from tissue spaces to the bloodstream and is a major part of the body’s immune system. The description in the question instead matches Spleen.

rationale: Spleen is the matching concept. In this reference context: An organ in the upper far left part of the abdomen, to the left of the stomach, which filters blood and is involved in immune response.

subject: NP2
stem:
In Reproductive Concepts, which concept matches this description?

Sexual activities that do not involve vaginal intercourse, which can help reduce the risk of pregnancy and STIs when no bodily fluids are exchanged.

options.rationale: Cervical caps: A barrier form of contraception made of silicone that is inserted into the vagina and fits over the cervix to prevent sperm from entering the uterus. The description in the question instead matches Outercourse.

Outercourse is the matching concept. In this reference context: Sexual activities that do not involve vaginal intercourse, which can help reduce the risk of pregnancy and STIs when no bodily fluids are exchanged.
Fimbriae: Finger-like projections at the end of the Fallopian tubes that help guide the egg from the ovary into the tube during ovulation. The description in the question instead matches Outercourse.

LGBTQIA+: An inclusive acronym that stands for Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transgender, Queer or Questioning, Intersex, Asexual, and other sexual orientations and gender identities. The description in the question instead matches Outercourse.

rationale: Outercourse is the matching concept. In this reference context: Sexual activities that do not involve vaginal intercourse, which can help reduce the risk of pregnancy and STIs when no bodily fluids are exchanged.

subject: CROSS

An infection caused by Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus that is difficult to treat because it exhibits resistance to nearly all available antibiotics.

options.rationale: Superinfection: A secondary infection in a client having a preexisting infection. C-diff and yeast infections as a result of antibiotic therapy are examples of superinfections. The description in the question instead matches Methicillin-resistant S. aureus.

Antifungal: Medications that are used to treat fungal infections. For example, nystatin is used to treat Candida albicans, a fungal infection. The description in the question instead matches Methicillin-resistant S. aureus.
Pathogen: An organism causing disease to its host. The description in the question instead matches Methicillin-resistant S. aureus.

Methicillin-resistant S. aureus is the matching concept. In this reference context: An infection caused by Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus that is difficult to treat because it exhibits resistance to nearly all available antibiotics.

Larger areas of purple or red discolorations on the skin, often caused by bleeding underneath the skin.

Psychotherapy that selects theoretical models or techniques from various therapeutic schools to suit the client’s particular problems.

subject: NP4
stem:
Which entry in the reference comparison “Common Medications for Management of Multiple Sclerosis” matches this information?

Mechanism of Action: Binds to WBCs to prevent further damage to the myelin.

options.rationale: Glatiramer acetate: A synthetic protein similar to myelin used to decrease the number of plaques and increase time between relapses. The description in the question instead matches IV monoclonal antibody.
The matching entry is IV monoclonal antibody. Mechanism of Action: Binds to WBCs to prevent further damage to the myelin.

Corticosteroids: Treat acute relapses. Shorten duration by exerting anti-inflammatory effects and acting on T cells and cytokines. The description in the question instead matches IV monoclonal antibody.
Baclofen or tizanidine: Muscle relaxant used to reduce muscle spasticity. The description in the question instead matches IV monoclonal antibody.

rationale: The matching entry is IV monoclonal antibody. Mechanism of Action: Binds to WBCs to prevent further damage to the myelin.

A procedure to restore blood flow through the artery by inserting and inflating a tiny balloon; it may also involve placing a stent to keep the artery open.

Pericardiocentesis: A procedure to remove fluid from the sac surrounding the heart. The description in the question instead matches Angioplasty.

The spread of malignant cells through the blood or lymphatic system and invasion in other areas of the body.

Chyle: A milky bodily fluid consisting of lymph and emulsified fats, absorbed from the intestines during digestion. The description in the question instead matches Metastasize.
Interstitial space: The space between individual cells in the tissues. The description in the question instead matches Metastasize.

Lymph nodes: Small bean-shaped organs located throughout the lymphatic system that store immune system cells and filter lymph fluid to remove foreign material. The description in the question instead matches Metastasize.

Type of anovulation associated with the natural aging process, as well as primary ovarian insufficiency (ovarian failure before the age of 40).

A system in the brain that controls pain and reward and addictive behaviors.

Opioid system is the matching concept. In this reference context: A system in the brain that controls pain and reward and addictive behaviors.
Norepinephrine and Epinephrine: Substances that stimulate alpha- and beta-receptors in the sympathetic nervous system. The description in the question instead matches Opioid system.

Sympathetic Nervous System receptors: Alpha-1, Alpha-2, Beta-1, and Beta-2 receptors that are stimulated by epinephrine and norepinephrine. The description in the question instead matches Opioid system.

subject: CROSS
stem:
In Integumentary System Terminology, which concept matches this description?

A band or sheet of connective tissue, primarily collagen, beneath the skin that attaches, stabilizes, encloses, and separates muscles, bones, and other internal organs.

options.rationale: Skin ulcer: An open sore on an external or internal surface of the body, caused by a break in the skin or mucous membrane that fails to heal. The description in the question instead matches Fascia.

Elastin: A protein in connective tissue that is elastic and allows many tissues in the body to resume their shape after stretching or contracting. The description in the question instead matches Fascia.

Fascia is the matching concept. In this reference context: A band or sheet of connective tissue, primarily collagen, beneath the skin that attaches, stabilizes, encloses, and separates muscles, bones, and other internal organs.

Scar: A mark left on the skin or within body tissue where a wound, burn, or sore has not healed completely, and fibrous connective tissue has developed. The description in the question instead matches Fascia.

rationale: Fascia is the matching concept. In this reference context: A band or sheet of connective tissue, primarily collagen, beneath the skin that attaches, stabilizes, encloses, and separates muscles, bones, and other internal organs.

subject: NP5
stem:
In Foundational Mental Health Concepts, which concept matches this description?

Mental illness that causes disabling functional impairment that substantially interferes with one or more major life activities. Examples of serious mental illnesses that commonly interfere with major life activities include major depressive disorder, schizophrenia, and bipolar disorder.

options.rationale: Trauma: An event, series of events, or set of circumstances that is experienced by an individual as physically or emotionally harmful and can have lasting adverse effects on the individual’s functioning and physical, social, emotional, or spiritual well-being. The description in the question instead matches Serious mental illness.

Suicide risk assessment: Identifying the risk of a client dying by suicide by assessing suicidal ideation, plan, intent, suicidal or self-harm behaviors, risk factors, and protective factors. The description in the question instead matches Serious mental illness.

Mental health: A state of well-being in which an individual realizes their own abilities, copes with the normal stresses of life, works productively, and contributes to their community. The description in the question instead matches Serious mental illness.

Serious mental illness is the matching concept. In this reference context: Mental illness that causes disabling functional impairment that substantially interferes with one or more major life activities. Examples of serious mental illnesses that commonly interfere with major life activities include major depressive disorder, schizophrenia, and bipolar disorder.

subject: CROSS
stem:
In Cardiovascular & Renal Systems, which concept matches this description?

A blood test that measures how long it takes for a client’s blood to clot. PT is used to monitor the effects of warfarin in preventing clot formation.

options.rationale: Prothrombin time is the matching concept. In this reference context: A blood test that measures how long it takes for a client’s blood to clot. PT is used to monitor the effects of warfarin in preventing clot formation.
Sensitivity analysis: A test performed in addition to a culture to select an effective antibiotic to treat a microorganism. The description in the question instead matches Prothrombin time.

Gram stain: A test used to quickly diagnose types of bacterial infection. Gram-positive and gram-negative bacteria stain differently because their cell walls are different. Identification of bacteria as gram-positive or gram-negative assists the health care provider in selecting an appropriate antibiotic to treat the infection. The description in the question instead matches Prothrombin time.
Fibrillation: An uncoordinated beating of the heart, which if serious and untreated, can lead to decreased cardiac output and death. The description in the question instead matches Prothrombin time.

rationale: Prothrombin time is the matching concept. In this reference context: A blood test that measures how long it takes for a client’s blood to clot. PT is used to monitor the effects of warfarin in preventing clot formation.

subject: NP4
stem:
In Nervous System Alterations, which concept matches this description?

Refers to damage to the bundle of nerves and nerve fibers that sends and receives signals from the brain.

options.rationale: Guillain-Barré syndrome: A rare autoimmune disease that causes muscle weakness and sometimes paralysis. The description in the question instead matches Spinal cord injury.

Epilepsy: A chronic disorder that is defined by at least two unprovoked seizures occurring at least 24 hours apart and in which groups of nerve cells, or neurons, in the brain sometimes send the wrong signals and cause recurrent, unpredictable, and unprovoked seizures. The description in the question instead matches Spinal cord injury.

Inflammation of the bronchi. It is most commonly caused by viruses, such as rhinovirus, influenza virus, or adenovirus. However, it can also be caused by bacteria or exposure to irritants like smoke or pollution.

Description: Significantly decreased interest or pleasure in almost all activities

Actions/Indications/Benefits: Increases clotting factors and expands blood volume. Indicated for clients with bleeding disorders, thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP), and life-threatening hemorrhage in patients who have significant coagulation deficiencies. Also used to reverse a client’s elevated INR when it needs to be brought down quickly to prevent complications from occurring. One unit increases clotting factors approximately 2-5%. The movement disorders include akathisia, dystonia, tics, and other abnormal involuntary movements.

Hypertensive crisis: A condition that can be caused by MAOIs with severe hypertension (blood pressure greater than 180/120 mm Hg) and evidence of organ dysfunction. Symptoms may include occipital headache (which may radiate frontally), palpitations, neck stiffness or soreness, nausea or vomiting, sweating, dilated pupils, photophobia, shortness of breath, or confusion. The description in the question instead matches Tardive dyskinesia.

Metabolic syndrome: A cluster of conditions that occur together, increasing the risk of heart disease, stroke, and type 2 diabetes. Symptoms include increased blood pressure, high blood sugar, excess body fat around the waist, and abnormal cholesterol or triglyceride levels. Weight, glucose levels, and lipid levels should be monitored regularly. The description in the question instead matches Tardive dyskinesia.

Extrapyramidal symptoms: Involuntary motor symptoms similar to those associated with Parkinson’s disease. Includes symptoms such as akathisia (distressing motor restlessness) and acute dystonia (painful muscle spasms). Often treated with anticholinergic medications such as benztropine and trihexyphenidyl. The description in the question instead matches Tardive dyskinesia.

stem:
Which entry in the reference comparison “Common Diagnostic Tests for Nervous System Disorders” matches this information?

Description and Indication: Provides imaging of the brain and spinal cord by using magnetic energy to detect strokes, multiple sclerosis, tumors, trauma, seizures, and brain herniation. Produces greater detail than CT with improved detail of intracranial structures, but the procedure takes longer to complete and may not be appropriate if a client is experiencing a life- threatening emergency.; Contrast agents, such as gadolinium, can be used with MRI to enhance visualization.

options.rationale: CT scan: Computer assisted X-ray that provides cross-sectional views of body parts. Used to detect problems such as hemorrhage, tumor, cyst, infarction, edema, brain atrophy, and other abnormalities. Contrast can be used to enhance visualization of brain structures, although scanning is typically first performed without contrast. The description in the question instead matches Magnetic resonance imaging.

The matching entry is Magnetic resonance imaging. Description and Indication: Provides imaging of the brain and spinal cord by using magnetic energy to detect strokes, multiple sclerosis, tumors, trauma, seizures, and brain herniation. Produces greater detail than CT with improved detail of intracranial structures, but the procedure takes longer to complete and may not be appropriate if a client is experiencing a life- threatening emergency.; Contrast agents, such as gadolinium, can be used with MRI to enhance visualization.

Electroencephalography: Electrodes are placed on the scalp to record electrical activity of the cerebral hemispheres. Each graphic recording represents electrical impulses within the brain. The frequency, amplitude, and characteristics of the brain waves are recorded to evaluate seizure disorders, cerebral disease, brain injury, and brain death. The description in the question instead matches Magnetic resonance imaging.

Electroneurography: Measures the conduction velocity of peripheral nerves. A brief electrical stimulus is initiated at the distal portion of the sensory nerve being tested. A recording of the depolarization wave is taken at a point proximal to the stimulus. The time between the initial stimulus and the beginning of the depolarization wave is measured (i.e., nerve conduction velocity). Damaged nerves will have slower conduction velocities. The description in the question instead matches Magnetic resonance imaging.

stem:
In Infection, which concept matches this description?

The disease stage after the incubation period when the pathogen continues to multiply and the host begins to experience general signs and symptoms of illness that result from activation of the immune system, such as fever, pain, soreness, swelling, or inflammation. Usually, such signs and symptoms are too general to indicate a particular disease.

options.rationale: Opportunistic pathogen: A pathogen that only causes disease in situations that compromise the host’s defenses, such as the body’s protective barriers, immune system, or normal microbiota. Individuals susceptible to opportunistic infections include the very young, the elderly, women who are pregnant, clients undergoing chemotherapy, people with immunodeficiencies (such as acquired immunodeficiency syndrome [AIDS]), clients who are recovering from surgery, and those who have had a breach of protective barriers (such as a severe wound or burn). The description in the question instead matches Prodromal period.

Specific adaptive immunity: The immune response that is activated when the nonspecific innate immune response is insufficient to control an infection. There are two types of adaptive responses: the cell-mediated immune response, which is carried out by T cells, and the humoral immune response, which is controlled by activated B cells and antibodies. The description in the question instead matches Prodromal period.

Standard precautions: The minimum infection prevention practices that apply to all client care, regardless of suspected or confirmed infection status of the client, in any setting where health care is delivered. The description in the question instead matches Prodromal period.

stem:

A client safety event that reaches a client and results in death, permanent harm, or severe temporary harm requiring interventions to sustain life.

options.rationale: Simple human error: According to the Just Culture model, this is an error that occurs when an individual inadvertently does something other than what should have been done. Learning Culture: A quality of an institutional culture of safety that demonstrates the willingness and the competence to draw the right conclusions from safety information systems, and the will to implement major reforms when their need is indicated. The description in the question instead matches Sentinel event.

stem:
In Oxygenation, which concept matches this description?

A technique helpful for clients who have difficulty coughing. Teach the client to inhale with a medium-sized breath and then make a sound like “ha” to push the air out quickly with the mouth slightly open.

options.rationale: Pursed-lip breathing: A breathing technique that encourages a person to inhale through the nose and exhale through the mouth at a slow, controlled flow. The description in the question instead matches Huffing technique.

Huffing technique is the matching concept. In this reference context: A technique helpful for clients who have difficulty coughing. Teach the client to inhale with a medium-sized breath and then make a sound like “ha” to push the air out quickly with the mouth slightly open.

Incentive spirometer: A medical device commonly prescribed after surgery to reduce the buildup of fluid in the lungs and to prevent pneumonia. While sitting upright, the client should breathe in slowly and deeply through the tubing with the goal of raising the piston to a specified level. The client should attempt to hold their breath for five seconds, or as long as tolerated, and then rest for a few seconds. This technique should be repeated by the client ten times every hour while awake. The description in the question instead matches Huffing technique.

Coughing and deep breathing: A breathing technique where the client is encouraged to take deep, slow breaths and then exhale slowly. After each set of breaths, the client should cough. This technique is repeated 3 to 5 times every hour. The description in the question instead matches Huffing technique.

rationale: Huffing technique is the matching concept. In this reference context: A technique helpful for clients who have difficulty coughing. Teach the client to inhale with a medium-sized breath and then make a sound like “ha” to push the air out quickly with the mouth slightly open.

In Substance Use Disorders, which concept matches this description?

A chronic illness caused by repeated misuse of psychoactive substances (e.g., alcohol, caffeine, cannabis, hallucinogens, inhalants, opioids, sedatives, hypnotics, anxiolytics, stimulants, and tobacco) that have a common effect of directly activating the brain’s reward system.

options.rationale: Delirium tremens: A rapid-onset, fluctuating disturbance of attention and cognition, sometimes associated with hallucinations, due to alcohol withdrawal. In its most severe manifestation, DTs are accompanied by agitation and signs of extreme autonomic hyperactivity, including fever, severe tachycardia, hypertension, and drenching sweats. DTs typically begin between 72 and 96 hours after the client’s last drink. The description in the question instead matches Substance use disorder.

Binge drinking: Consuming several standard drinks on one occasion in the past 30 days, defined for males as drinking five or more standard alcoholic drinks on one occasion, and for females as drinking four or more standard drinks on one occasion. The description in the question instead matches Substance use disorder.

Substance use disorder is the matching concept. In this reference context: A chronic illness caused by repeated misuse of psychoactive substances (e.g., alcohol, caffeine, cannabis, hallucinogens, inhalants, opioids, sedatives, hypnotics, anxiolytics, stimulants, and tobacco) that have a common effect of directly activating the brain’s reward system.

Withdrawal management: Interventions that manage the physical and emotional symptoms that occur after a person stops using a psychoactive substance; also referred to as detoxification. Withdrawal symptoms vary in intensity and duration based on the substance(s) used, the duration and amount of use, and the overall health of the individual. The description in the question instead matches Substance use disorder.

rationale: Substance use disorder is the matching concept. A condition arising when the body is deprived of oxygen, causing unconsciousness or death; suffocation.

options.rationale: Lung cancer: A type of cancer that begins in the lungs and may spread to lymph nodes or other organs in the body. The description in the question instead matches Asphyxia.
Asphyxia is the matching concept. In this reference context: A condition arising when the body is deprived of oxygen, causing unconsciousness or death; suffocation.
Metastases: The spread of cancer from one part of the body to another. The description in the question instead matches Asphyxia.

Emphysema: A chronic respiratory disease where there is overinflation of the air sacs (alveoli) in the lungs, leading to a decrease in lung function and breathlessness. The description in the question instead matches Asphyxia.

rationale: Asphyxia is the matching concept. In this reference context: A condition arising when the body is deprived of oxygen, causing unconsciousness or death; suffocation.

subject: NP2
stem:
Which entry in the reference comparison “Diagnostic Tests for Diagnosing Congenital Heart Defects and Rationale” matches this information?

Rationale: Involves inhalation of a radioactive gas to examine the airways, followed by injection of an isotope intravenously, which is then scanned and tracked to determine blood flow and flow patterns through the lung vessels.

options.rationale: The matching entry is Ventilation-Perfusion Scan. Rationale: Involves inhalation of a radioactive gas to examine the airways, followed by injection of an isotope intravenously, which is then scanned and tracked to determine blood flow and flow patterns through the lung vessels.

Chest X-ray: A radiographic image of the chest that shows normal anatomy, as well as any abnormal findings such as pulmonary congestion, abnormal heart location, size, or shape. The description in the question instead matches Ventilation-Perfusion Scan.

Magnetic Resonance Imaging: Imaging obtained by placing the infant or child in a machine that emits a strong magnetic field that surrounds the body. This imaging takes an hour or more and allows visualization of any cardiac shunts, valve function, heart structures, and thickness of myocardial walls. The description in the question instead matches Ventilation-Perfusion Scan.

Holter Monitor: A portable ECG device that the client wears that records electrical activity of the heart over a period of time, usually 24-48 hours, on an outpatient basis. The client or parent presses a button to record events such as shortness of breath or palpitations. The recording shows arrhythmias and any other normal or abnormal electrical activity that occurs during these recorded events. The description in the question instead matches Ventilation-Perfusion Scan.

rationale: The matching entry is Ventilation-Perfusion Scan. Rationale: Involves inhalation of a radioactive gas to examine the airways, followed by injection of an isotope intravenously, which is then scanned and tracked to determine blood flow and flow patterns through the lung vessels.

Deep tissue pressure injuries: Persistent; non-blanchable; deep red, maroon, or purple discoloration of intact or nonintact skin revealing a dark wound bed or blood-filled blister. Pain and temperature change often precede skin color changes. Discoloration may appear differently in darkly pigmented skin. The description in the question instead matches Stage 1 pressure injuries.

Primary intention: A type of wound that is sutured, stapled, glued, or otherwise closed so the wound heals beneath the closure. The description in the question instead matches Stage 1 pressure injuries.

In Autonomic Nervous System, which concept matches this description?

Postganglionic neuron where neurotransmitters norepinephrine and epinephrine are released. Includes alpha (α)-receptors and beta (β)-receptors.

options.rationale: Adrenergic is the matching concept. In this reference context: Postganglionic neuron where neurotransmitters norepinephrine and epinephrine are released. Includes alpha (α)-receptors and beta (β)-receptors.

Chronotropic: Drugs may change the heart rate and rhythm by affecting the electrical conduction system of the heart and the nerves that influence it, such as by changing the rhythm (increasing) produced by the sinoatrial node. Positive chronotropes increase heart rate; negative chronotropes decrease heart rate. The description in the question instead matches Adrenergic.

Cholinergic: Postganglionic neuron where acetylcholine (ACh) is released that stimulates nicotinic receptors and muscarinic receptors. Also relating to drugs that inhibit, enhance, or mimic the action of ACh. The description in the question instead matches Adrenergic.
Autonomic nervous system: Controls cardiac and smooth muscle, as well as glandular tissue; associated with involuntary responses. The description in the question instead matches Adrenergic.

Sinuses: Mucus production; decrease the weight of the skull. The description in the question instead matches Lungs.
Diaphragm: Contracts and relaxes to change the volume of the thoracic cavity to allow for breathing. The description in the question instead matches Lungs.

subject: NP2
stem:
In Reproductive Concepts, which concept matches this description?

A viral STI caused by the herpes simplex virus (HSV). It results in painful sores or blisters on the genitals, rectum, or mouth. There is no cure, but antiviral medications can reduce symptoms and transmission.

options.rationale: Irregular bleeding: Unpredictable menstrual bleeding that occurs at irregular intervals. The description in the question instead matches Genital herpes.

Epispadias: A congenital abnormality in which the urethra opens on the upper surface of the penis instead of at the tip. It can also occur in females, where the urethra opens too far anteriorly. The description in the question instead matches Genital herpes.

Genital herpes is the matching concept. In this reference context: A viral STI caused by the herpes simplex virus (HSV). It results in painful sores or blisters on the genitals, rectum, or mouth. There is no cure, but antiviral medications can reduce symptoms and transmission.

Alpha-fetoprotein: A protein produced in the liver of a developing fetus, often measured in prenatal tests to assess the risk of fetal abnormalities. The description in the question instead matches Genital herpes.

rationale: Genital herpes is the matching concept. In this reference context: A viral STI caused by the herpes simplex virus (HSV). It results in painful sores or blisters on the genitals, rectum, or mouth. There is no cure, but antiviral medications can reduce symptoms and transmission.

stem:
In Digestive System Terminology, which concept matches this description?

Small, finger-like projections that protrude from the epithelial lining of the intestinal wall, increasing the surface area for absorption.

options.rationale: Probiotics: Live bacteria and yeasts that are good for your health, especially your digestive system. The description in the question instead matches Villi.
Defecation: The final step in digestion when undigested materials are expelled from the body as feces. The description in the question instead matches Villi.
Visceral: Relating to the internal organs of the body, especially those in the abdomen. The description in the question instead matches Villi.
Villi is the matching concept. In this reference context: Small, finger-like projections that protrude from the epithelial lining of the intestinal wall, increasing the surface area for absorption.

Binding written, verbal, or implied agreements.

Normal stress: Stress (also referred to as “eustress”) that does not have lasting consequences and is successfully managed by the individual who is experiencing it. The description in the question instead matches Contracts.
Shared governance: A shared leadership model between management and employees working together to achieve common goals. The description in the question instead matches Contracts.

subject: NP4
stem:
In Endocrine System Terminology, which concept matches this description?

An organ with both exocrine and endocrine functions, producing digestive enzymes and hormones like insulin and glucagon.

options.rationale: Adrenocorticotropic hormone: A hormone produced by the pituitary gland, stimulating the adrenal cortex to produce cortisol and other hormones. The description in the question instead matches Pancreas.

Pineal gland: A small cone-shaped structure in the brain that produces melatonin, influencing reproductive development and physiological cycles. The description in the question instead matches Pancreas.
Calcitonin: A hormone produced by the thyroid gland that helps regulate calcium levels in the blood by reducing the concentration of calcium. The description in the question instead matches Pancreas.
Pancreas is the matching concept. In this reference context: An organ with both exocrine and endocrine functions, producing digestive enzymes and hormones like insulin and glucagon.

rationale: Pancreas is the matching concept. In this reference context: An organ with both exocrine and endocrine functions, producing digestive enzymes and hormones like insulin and glucagon.

subject: NP5
stem:
In Eating Disorders, which concept matches this description?

Individuals severely limit the amount and type of food they consume and may engage in excessive exercise.

options.rationale: Binge-eating/Purging type: Individuals experience episodes of binge eating and/or purging. The description in the question instead matches Restricting type.

Family-based therapy: A type of psychotherapy in which parents take an active role in managing their child’s eating behaviors and weight restoration. The description in the question instead matches Restricting type.
Restricting type is the matching concept. In this reference context: Individuals severely limit the amount and type of food they consume and may engage in excessive exercise.

Refeeding syndrome: A potentially fatal complication for any client with negligible food intake for more than five days that involves hypophosphatemia; serious sodium and fluid imbalances; changes in glucose, protein, and fat metabolism; thiamine deficiency; hypokalemia; and hypomagnesaemia. The description in the question instead matches Restricting type.

rationale: Restricting type is the matching concept. In this reference context: Individuals severely limit the amount and type of food they consume and may engage in excessive exercise.

subject: CROSS

Standards describing a competent level of behavior in the professional nursing role, including activities related to ethics, advocacy, respectful and equitable practice, communication, collaboration, leadership, education, scholarly inquiry, quality of practice, professional practice evaluation, resource stewardship, and environmental health.

options.rationale: Interprofessional collaborative practice: Multiple health workers from different professional backgrounds working together with clients, families, caregivers, and communities to deliver the highest quality of care. Nurse residency programs: Provide additional professional development support for all newly licensed nurses but vary from institution to institution. Resiliency training: Educational sessions that foster feelings of mindfulness and sensitivity to self and cultivate professional development techniques that contribute to long-term engagement in the profession. Occurs due to exposure to various chemicals, drugs, and products encountered in everyday life.

options.rationale: Anaphylaxis: A life-threatening Type I hypersensitivity reaction that occurs rapidly and systemically, and if not promptly treated, it can be fatal. The description in the question instead matches Chemical carcinogenesis.

Syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone: When cancerous tumors produce excessive antidiuretic hormone. Can also be caused by some chemotherapy medications. Leads to water retention. The description in the question instead matches Chemical carcinogenesis.
Chemical carcinogenesis is the matching concept. In this reference context: Occurs due to exposure to various chemicals, drugs, and products encountered in everyday life.

Tonsils: Lymphoid nodules located along the inner surface of the pharynx and are important in developing immunity to oral pathogens. The description in the question instead matches Chemical carcinogenesis.

A laceration of the labia and perineum affects the skin and subcutaneous tissue.

Massage: A physical manipulation of tissue that can be provided in different ways, depending upon the preference of the laboring client. The description in the question instead matches First-degree laceration.
Dilation: The gradual opening of the cervix, measured in centimeters (cm), from 0 to 10 cm. The description in the question instead matches First-degree laceration.

stem:
In Oxygenation, which concept matches this description?

Refers to the exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide in the alveoli and the pulmonary capillaries; also called respiration.

options.rationale: PaO2: Partial pressure of dissolved oxygen in arterial blood indicated in an ABG result. Normal range is 80-100 mmHg. The description in the question instead matches Gas exchange.
Bradypnea: Decreased respiratory rate less than the normal range according to the client’s age. The description in the question instead matches Gas exchange.
Gas exchange is the matching concept. In this reference context: Refers to the exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide in the alveoli and the pulmonary capillaries; also called respiration.
Saturation of peripheral oxygen: Hemoglobin saturation level measured by pulse oximetry. Normal range is 94-98%. The description in the question instead matches Gas exchange.

rationale: Gas exchange is the matching concept. In this reference context: Refers to the exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide in the alveoli and the pulmonary capillaries; also called respiration.

The fetal heart rate shows slight fluctuations of 5 bpm or less.

In Endocrine System Terminology, which concept matches this description?

A surgical procedure to remove one or more of the parathyroid glands.

options.rationale: Hypophysectomy: Surgical removal of the pituitary gland. The description in the question instead matches Parathyroidectomy.

Endocrine surgeons: Medical specialists who perform surgical procedures on the endocrine glands, such as the thyroid, parathyroid, and adrenal glands, to treat various endocrine disorders and diseases. The description in the question instead matches Parathyroidectomy.

Radioactive iodine uptake: A diagnostic test that measures how much radioactive iodine is absorbed by the thyroid gland, used to evaluate thyroid function. The description in the question instead matches Parathyroidectomy.

Irregularities in a person’s heart rate and/or rhythm.

Description: Adoptive parents legally take a child into their family and raise them as their own because of infertility issues or because they prefer adoption. Adoption may be open or closed. Open adoption ranges from simply knowing the identities of the birth parent(s) to having a continued relationship with the birth parents as the child grows up. Closed adoption means the family does not have access to information about the birth parent(s) nor do birth parents have access to information about the adoptive family or child.

options.rationale: Families who experience housing insecurity: Some children are raised in families that do not have a stable home or are homeless. Families may experience housing insecurity due to the parents’ loss of a job or steady income, bankruptcy, or other issues. They may be living in a car, hotel, homeless shelter, or multiple dwellings with friends and extended family. Family members experiencing housing insecurity or homelessness often do not share this status with others due to the shame and embarrassment that results from social stigma. The description in the question instead matches Adoptive families.

The death of most or all of the cells in an organ or tissue due to disease, injury, or failure of the blood supply causing the skin to turn black.

options.rationale: Psoriasis: A chronic autoimmune skin disease that speeds up the growth cycle of skin cells, causing red, itchy, scaly patches on the body, most commonly on the elbows, knees, and scalp. The description in the question instead matches Necrosis.
Blister: A small bubble on the skin filled with serum and caused by friction, burning, or other damage. The description in the question instead matches Necrosis.
Gangrene: The death of body tissue due to a lack of blood flow or a bacterial infection. The description in the question instead matches Necrosis.

stem:
In Lymphatic & Immune Systems Terminology, which concept matches this description?

A surgical procedure to remove all or part of a lymph node, usually performed if the lymph node is large enough to be felt on physical exam.

options.rationale: Sentinel lymph node biopsy: A procedure used to find the best lymph nodes to biopsy, involving the injection of a radioactive tracer or dye near the tumor. The description in the question instead matches Open lymph node biopsy.

Laparoscopic lymph node biopsy: A minimally invasive procedure performed under general anesthesia, where a small tube with a light and camera is used to remove lymph node tissue. The description in the question instead matches Open lymph node biopsy.

Open lymph node biopsy is the matching concept. In this reference context: A surgical procedure to remove all or part of a lymph node, usually performed if the lymph node is large enough to be felt on physical exam.

Adenoidectomy: The surgical removal of the adenoid, which is located behind the nasal cavity, often performed along with a tonsillectomy. The description in the question instead matches Open lymph node biopsy.
